articles.title: Motorista passa mal e capota carro em São Sebastião do Paraíso | G1
articles.standfirst: Condutora de 62 anos foi socorrida pelo SAMU após colisão entre um Volkswagen Gol e um Toyota Corolla no bairro Mocoquinha.
articles.summary: Após sofrer um mal-estar, condutora de 62 anos colidiu contra outro veículo e capotou no bairro Mocoquinha; ela foi levada à Santa Casa de São Sebastião do Paraíso.
articles.body:
Uma mulher de 62 anos ficou ferida após se envolver em um acidente de trânsito na tarde desta terça-feira (10), em São Sebastião do Paraíso (MG). A ocorrência foi registrada por volta das 14h50 no cruzamento entre a Travessa da Bahia e a Rua Raul Soares, no bairro Mocoquinha, e mobilizou equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros, do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU), da Polícia Militar e da Guarda Civil Municipal.

Segundo informações da condutora de um Volkswagen Gol, ela seguia pela Travessa da Bahia quando sofreu um mal-estar e não conseguiu precisar o que aconteceu em seguida. De acordo com o relato, o veículo cruzou a via preferencial e colidiu com um Toyota Corolla.

O motorista do Corolla não sofreu ferimentos. Conforme informou aos bombeiros, após a colisão o Gol ainda atingiu o meio-fio da calçada, capotou e ficou com as quatro rodas voltadas para cima.

Motorista passa mal, provoca acidente e capota carro em cruzamento de São Sebastião do Paraíso — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Antes da chegada das equipes de resgate, um bombeiro militar de folga que passava pelo local prestou os primeiros socorros à vítima.

Quando as equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros chegaram ao local, profissionais do Samu já haviam conseguido acessar a condutora e retirá-la pela porta do automóvel, sem necessidade de procedimentos de desencarceramento.

Após ser imobilizada e estabilizada, a mulher foi encaminhada pela equipe médica do SAMU para a emergência da Santa Casa de Misericórdia de São Sebastião do Paraíso.

A Polícia Militar e a Guarda Civil Municipal também estiveram no local e adotaram as providências relacionadas à ocorrência, incluindo o controle e a segurança do trânsito.

Ahí Fermín dobla a Güler (7-3), que también pierde el duelo de la asistencias (5-4). Solo la explosión del madridista, con 55 puntazos en cuatro jornadas, y su regularidad jornada a jornada ha equilibrado la batalla por el reinado Fantasy de los centrocampistas. En la Champions también están empatados (23 puntos), aunque Arda los sumó en solo dos partidos y Fermín en los cuatro. Cualquiera de los dos es un titular indiscutible.. El debate Güler-Fermín, los mejores fichajes del mercado, el repaso a sus ligas oficiales y, sobre todo, el intercambio de experiencias entre los dos últimos campeones del Movistar Fantasy MARCA. articles.title: Peterborough United: Robbie Savage rejects commentary work criticism
articles.summary: Robbie Savage rejects criticism that his work as a co-commentator and pundit is impacting his role as Peterborough United boss.
articles.body:
Peterborough United boss Robbie Savage has rejected criticism of his work as a co-commentator and pundit as "a narrative that gets created if we're not winning games".

Savage was appointed on 2 October and won his first two games in charge but Posh have failed to win any of their past six games.

Before Saturday's 5-0 home defeat by Reading in the FA Cup, Savage co-commentated for TNT's coverage of AEK Athens v Real Madrid and Oxford City v Leicester City on Wednesday and Friday respectively.

The 52-year-old has also continued to present 606 on BBC Radio 5 Live, although did not feature on the post-match reaction show last weekend.

But Savage said his "commitment" to the League One club was absolute, telling the club's in-house media , external he was "first one in and last one to leave".

Since the 3-1 win at Leicester City on 10 October, Peterborough have drawn two and lost two of their next four league games to fall back to 22nd in the table.

They also missed out on a place in the quarter-finals of the EFL Cup after they were knocked out by fellow third-tier side Bradford City on 27 October.

Savage, who played as a midfielder for clubs including Derby County, Birmingham City, Leicester City and Blackburn Rovers, succeeded Luke Williams as Posh boss having previously managed Forest Green Rovers and Macclesfield.

"It's all about winning games of football," added Savage. "The narrative can be spun in any way but I'm a football man.

"It's my life. It's what I love doing and I love watching football. I'm not somebody who goes home and sits in front of the TV, or goes to the pub or has any hobbies outside of football.

"I'm not a golfer. I just love football. I'll go and watch every game that I can.

"I'm very fortunate that when I go and do games for TNT or 606, I'm getting knowledge all the time."

Savage added that he had also recently attended the games of local sides including Peterborough Sports and Wisbech Town.

"I put my hood up, I go to games, I pay to go in because I want to give back to grassroots football clubs," he said. "I go and watch every single game of football I can, I go and watch league games, because I love it.

"It hurts the fans the most when we lose, it hurts me a lot. But it's a narrative that gets created if we're not winning games of football.

"The bottom line is let's win games of football and then it all goes away."

articles.title: La Federación Vasca reclama al CSD la oficialidad de la Euskal Selekzioa
articles.standfirst: La iniciativa se sustenta a partir del articulado de la Ley del Deporte aprobada en 2022
articles.summary: La iniciativa se sustenta a partir del articulado de la Ley del Deporte aprobada en 2022
articles.body: La Federación Vasca de Fútbol (FVF) mantiene su empeño por lograr la oficialidad que Euskadi ya dispone en otras modalidades como Pelota, deporte en el que compite en Mundiales. La institución que dirige Iker Goñi ha solicitado al Consejo Superior de Deportes (CSD) que impulse la vía prevista en el artículo 48.2 de la Ley 39/2022 del Deporte, basada en el arraigo histórico y social de la modalidad deportiva. La pretensión de la FVF es conseguir disputar torneos oficiales de ámbito internacional en todas sus categorías y además del CSD también ha elevado la petición a la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF). La fundamentación federativa se articula a partir del “artículo 48.2 de la Ley 39/2022, de 30 de diciembre, del Deporte. Este precepto contempla que las federaciones deportivas autonómicas puedan participar directamente en el ámbito internacional cuando la federación internacional correspondiente lo permita y se trate de modalidades o especialidades deportivas con arraigo histórico y social en su comunidad autónoma”. En el argumentario de la EFF-FVF se destaca que “el fútbol vasco reúne una trayectoria histórica y una implantación social que justifican esta solicitud. Para fundamentar su petición, la federación aportará documentos históricos y sociales que documenten el arraigo de la práctica futbolística, el papel de los clubes, la trayectoria de sus selecciones y su dimensión social e institucional”. En esa carrera hacia la oficialidad contará con el apoyo del Gobierno Vasco, que en el compromiso 57 del programa de gobierno se especifica “la internacionalización de las selecciones nacionales y apoyar a las selecciones deportivas vascas que opten por avanzar en la oficialidad de sus selecciones para participar en campeonatos oficiales internacionales, tomando en consideración el marco del acuerdo alcanzado con el Gobierno español”. La Federación Vasca de Fútbol hace coincidir su petición con la nueva denominación para sus selecciones, que ahora atienden a la Euskal Selekzioa, y que este sábado se enfrentará a Venezuela en San Mamés. El compromiso de los federativos es ampliar al máximo la influencia de la selección, que antes del amistoso de San Mamés realizarán dos entrenamientos: el jueves lo harán en Lezama y el viernes se trasladarán a San Juan de Luz (Iparralde) para extender más todavía su reivindicación.

articles.title: El Barcelona regresa al Camp Nou con ánimo de revancha: "Este equipo no necesita recordar el pasado ni buscar motivaciones"
articles.standfirst: Se enfrenta a un Arsenal ante el que cayó en la final de la Champions League de 2025
articles.summary: Se enfrenta a un Arsenal ante el que cayó en la final de la Champions League de 2025
articles.body: El Barcelona recibe este jueves (18:45 horas) al Arsenal en el Camp Nou. Será la décima ocasión que el equipo femenino juegue en el coliseo azulgrana, donde no conoce la derrota, y la sexta vez que se mida al conjunto gunner, siendo el último precedente la final de la Champions League perdida en Lisboa en 2025. "Este equipo no necesita recordar el pasado ni buscar motivaciones. Jugar contra el Arsenal en el Camp Nou es suficiente motivación como para volver dos años atrás. Es un partido muy importante. Cuando te enfrentas a un rival de renombre, para nosotras es muy importante ofrecer un buen nivel e ir a por la victoria", aseguró Aitana Bonmatí. El equipo que dirige Pere Romeu visita por primera vez el Camp Nou esta temporada. El histórico en el coliseo azulgrana es positivo (ocho victorias y un empate), no tanto el balance con el que va a ser su rival: dos victorias y tres derrotas frente al Arsenal. La última de ellas, con el catalán en el banquillo azulgrana, sirvió de acicate para que el curso pasado se desquitaran con un póker histórico -ganando la Liga, la Copa de la Reina, la Supercopa de España y la Champions League- aún sin ser perfecto por no cruzarse con el conjunto inglés en el camino. Ahora tienen la oportunidad. "A pesar de haber ganado tanto, seguimos actuando como si nunca hubiéramos ganado nada. Las ganas y la ambición, así como el respeto que nos tenemos unos a otros, tanto jugadores como cuerpo técnico, son los aspectos de este equipo de los que me siento más orgulloso", expuso el técnico. El Barcelona llega a la cita como líder destacado (único con pleno de victorias) en una fase Liga de la estamos en el ecuador. Las azulgrana golearon al Paris FC (5-2), Roma (0-6) y HB Køge (0-8) en la primera mitad. "Jugamos contra un grandísimo equipo, con muy buenas futbolistas. Juegan muy bien y tienen el modelo de juego muy claro. Es un partido que tiene su dificultad y lo afrontaremos sabiendo que nos enfrentamos a un gran equipo y que tendremos que hacer las cosas muy bien", destacó el técnico azulgrana, que no podrá contar para la ocasión con Vicky López, Kerolin Nicoli, Kika Nazareth ni Laia Aleixandri. "Hemos repartido las cargas de la mejor forma posible. Las lesiones nos están ocupando mucho tiempo saber por qué está sucediendo", subrayó. El Arsenal, por su parte, se impuso al HB Køge (1-0) y Benfica (3-0), empatando su único partido a domicilio ante el Paris FC (2-2), ocupando de momento una tercera posición que permitiría al conjunto dirigido por Renée Slegers clasificarse directamente para los cuartos de final. El duelo también podría marcar el regreso de Mariona Caldentey y Ona Batlle al Camp Nou, si bien la primera está lesionada y la segunda es duda en el conjunto inglés. Sí está disponible Misa Rodríguez, exguardameta del Real Madrid y desde el verano en Inglaterra.

articles.title: Aberdeen: Who are the main candidates for the vacant manager's job?
articles.summary: Two domestic names stand out, while there is also the possibility of a foreign appointment following Stephen Robinson's departure.
articles.body:
Another season, another managerial sacking at Aberdeen.

Stephen Robinson's departure on Monday made it five dismissals since the spring of 2021.

The Northern Irishman followed Stephen Glass, Jim Goodwin, Barry Robson and Jimmy Thelin in making an abrupt exit on the watch of chairman Dave Cormack.

Most of the quintet have lasted less than a year and, although Thelin ended the Dons' 35-year wait to win the Scottish Cup, the general trend has been one of perceived underachievement in Scottish Premiership.

Derek McInnes, now with Rangers after spells at Kilmarnock and Heart of Midlothian, was the last Pittodrie boss to regularly deliver consistent results in the top flight and consequent European qualification.

So who could be next? And what qualities does such a manager require?

'Aberdeen hunt yet another manager after ill-fated Robinson reign'

Aberdeen sack Robinson after league slump

Falkirk add goals and grit to McGlynn's guile on rapid rise

Two names mentioned fairly early on after Robinson's exit were Dundee's Steven Pressley and Falkirk's John McGlynn .

Both have impressed in the Premiership this past 17 months, drawing admirers for style of play and good results.

Falkirk are third in the division, two places above Dundee, and McGlynn's side were sixth last season, again two places higher than Pressley's men.

Former Aberdeen defender Richard Foster said the pair are "the two that stand out for me domestically" and said of Elgin-born Pressley on BBC Radio Scotland's Breakfast: "I know he's got a quiet, laid-back demeanour, but I think in the dressing room, he commands respect.

"The players at Dundee seem to love playing for him.

"He knows the game very well. Having played at Hearts, having played at Celtic, he knows what it's like to be at a huge club."

Former Hearts, Hibernian and Scotland midfielder Michael Stewart has been impressed with McGlynn's track record of signing players.

Speaking on McGlynn on BBC Radio Scotland's Sportsound, Stewart said: "John McGlynn puts the miles in.

"He's up and down the road down south. He's up and around all over Scotland. He knows what the players are that are perhaps not in the eye of many others. He knows them intimately before they arrive at Falkirk.

"So it's no great surprise that his success rate with recruitment is pretty, pretty good.

"I would not be surprised if, whenever one or two of the bigger jobs start coming up... rather than being sort of an outsider, I think he'll be right in the hunt for some of those jobs."

Former Celtic and Hibs midfielder Scott Allan says McGlynn is "very tactically astute" and commented: "I love everything that John McGlynn does. Everybody in Scottish football can respect the job he's done there, the consistency.

"He's one of the most prepared managers, if not the most prepared manager for any sort of set-up that he faces week-to-week and he's shown that.

"It's a fantastic job he's done over the last three or four years. He deserves all the credit that comes his way."

It may seem like a lifetime ago, but it's actually only been five months since Steve Clarke stepped down as Scotland head coach.

The 63-year-old, like McGlynn, has vast coaching experience, including in Scotland after a two-year spell with Kilmarnock.

Clarke oversaw three qualifications to major tournaments with Scotland, ending long waits to appear at the European Championship and World Cup.

As well as managerial stints at West Bromwich Albion and Reading, Clarke has worked at Chelsea, Liverpool and Newcastle United, so little would daunt the former right-back.

Appointing Clarke would be a statement by Aberdeen and the challenge of restoring the club to competitiveness may be a compelling one for the man himself.

However, along with McGlynn, geography may play a part and their candidacy could depend on whether personal circumstances allow a switch to the north east.

Wigan Athletic boss and former Scotland centre-half Gary Caldwell has also been linked with the Pittodrie job. The 44-year-old cut his managerial teeth with the Latics and returned there earlier this year after spells in charge of Chesterfield, Partick Thistle and Exeter City.

Swede Thelin stands out as one of the few overseas managers Aberdeen have had.

Yes, Goodwin and Robinson hail from Ireland and Northern Ireland respectively, but both are very much embedded in Scottish football after spending so much time at various clubs north of the border.

The only other non-Scottish manager to grace the Pittodrie home dugout was the Dane, Ebbe Skovdahl, from 1999-2002.

As such, it is fair to say Aberdeen have not experimented too much with foreign coaches and have tended to go with faces familiar to the Scottish top flight.

With a German, Lutz Pfannenstiel, as the sporting director, Aberdeen look further afield this time?

It has become the vogue in the Premiership of late, with Hearts, Hibs and Motherwell going foreign, with Belgian Wouter Vrancken, Dutchman Marink Reedijk and Swede Alfred Johansson in recent months.

Should Pfannenstiel unearth the next Jens Berthel Askou, formerly of Motherwell, Dons fans will be delighted.

Podcast: What is going wrong at Aberdeen?

Former Aberdeen defender Stuart Duff is in interim charge of Aberdeen following the departures of Robinson, assistant Brian Kerr and coach Stephen Craigan.

The Dons are second bottom of the Premiership, two points above Kilmarnock.

Unless an appointment is made during the international break, Duff faces taking Aberdeen to face Kilmarnock on 21 November before visiting Rangers three days later, with their next home game being against Dundee on 28 November.

Confidence is low after seven league defeats so far this season, but the tightly-packed middle section of the league means Aberdeen are only a couple of wins off the top six.

articles.title: Valverde: "Trato de ser el mejor en mi posición... y en este momento estoy jugando de lateral"
articles.standfirst: El uruguayo también reconoció que no está "al cien por cien" por problemas físicos
articles.summary: El uruguayo también reconoció que no está "al cien por cien" por problemas físicos
articles.body: Federico Valverde reconoció que sigue con molestias físicas a su llegada a Uruguay para incorporarse a la selección, que afrontará los partidos de este parón de noviembre ante Argentina y República Dominicana. El futbolista del Real Madrid habló también de la nueva etapa con Diego Forlán y de su disposición a jugar donde lo necesite el entrenador. "Tuve una lesión antes de la convocatoria anterior, sigo con molestias, no estoy al 100%, pero a la Selección siempre hay que venir. Siempre es bueno estar acá y vivir el día a día con el grupo, conocer el método del entrenador. Tenía muchas ganas de estar aquí", señaló en el Aeropuerto Internacional de Carrasco. Valverde expresó su satisfacción por volver a la convocatoria y reencontrarse con Forlán, con quien coincidió como jugador en Peñarol: "Estoy muy feliz, hacía mucho que no venía y estoy contento de volver a estar con el equipo, con la Selección, con mis compañeros. Feliz también de poder disfrutar de un ídolo como Diego Forlán, con quien me tocó compartir como compañero de equipo en Peñarol, y hoy me toca vivirlo como entrenador. Voy a tratar de sacarle el mayor jugo cada día". Sobre la conversación que mantuvo con el seleccionador, explicó que trataron su estado y la etapa que comienza después del Mundial. "Hablamos de cómo me sentía yo, de que hay que cambiar la pisada de lo que sucedió anteriormente en el Mundial, de meter buena energía, de estar unidos como grupo, que cada uno aporte desde su lugar y que podamos darle alegrías a la gente de Uruguay", afirmó. El madridista manifestó su intención de aportar a la selección lo mismo que a su club: "Siempre intento hacer en Uruguay lo mismo que hago en mi club. Yo voy a tratar de aportar mi granito de arena para el equipo, aportar mi energía y tratar de que Uruguay obtenga victorias". Preguntado por su posición, Valverde aseguró que se adapta a las decisiones del técnico y se refirió a su papel como lateral en el Real Madrid. "Me preparo donde el entrenador quiera que juegue. Trato de ser el mejor en mi posición, en este momento estoy jugando de lateral y me preparo para hacer las cosas bien ahí y ser el mejor en mi posición. Me gusta ponerme retos nuevos, nuevos desafíos. Si después en la Selección me toca jugar en otro lado, daré lo mejor para que a Uruguay le vaya bien", concluyó.

articles.title: Jordon Hudson files lawsuit over leaked Ring videos that revealed her relationship with Bill Belichick in 2023
articles.summary: Belichick and Hudson reportedly broke up in late 2025.
articles.body:
Jordon Hudson has filed a lawsuit against the owners of a Massachusetts AirBnB over the Ring camera footage from the residence that showed her with former Patriots and current North Carolina coach Bill Belichick in 2023.

The suit, filed in a Massachusetts Superior Court, is seeking financial damages for what Hudson says includes "ridicule and denigration" because the "unwanted scrutiny and the ensuing media stories, which contain false information, has caused significant damage to Ms. Hudson."

The relationship between Hudson and Belichick was not publicly known at the time the Ring videos became public. The couple is no longer together and reportedly broke up approximately a year ago, though Hudson continues to be involved with Belichick's business affairs and is still a presence at UNC. Their breakup was reportedly so quiet that some around them did not know they were no longer together.

Hudson was the one who rented the AirBnB in 2023 for four nights. In her suit, Hudson says that Elise McDevitt, one of the owners of the AirBnB, texted her a video of the two.

"As we discussed, I'm a huge cowboys fan, but don't live under a rock!" McDevitt texted Hudson, according to the complaint. Hudson said she didn't understand. "It's clear who is on the video...I'll leave it at that," McDevitt said in a separate text. The complaint said that Hudson asked the hosts to delete the video after she checked out. "We will delete it from ring, but as you know, unfortunately, videos are never totally deleted," McDevitt responded, according to the complaint.

The complaint said that Hudson asked the hosts to delete the video after she checked out. "We will delete it from ring, but as you know, unfortunately, videos are never totally deleted," McDevitt responded, according to the complaint.

Hudson said that McDevitt also admitted to sending the video to other people; Hudson says that McDevitt and co-defendant Craig Nolan told her they did not release the video publicly.

Belichick was shirtless in the video, and the subsequent jokes about his lack of a shirt are also cited as a reason for the suit.

The Ring footage of a shirtless Belichick appeared online in November 2023 and immediately "went viral" and "became infamous," according to the civil complaint. That, the suit said, was "evidenced by the fact that football player Tom Brady made a highly-publicized joke about it during his roast on Netflix," which aired in May 2024, "six months after the video was initially leaked."

Hudson's alleged role at North Carolina was also the subject of much discussion after Belichick was hired as the Tar Heels coach in December of 2024. As part of a "Pablo Torre Finds Out" podcast investigation into the influence that Hudson had at North Carolina, Torre interviewed both McDevitt and Nolan. The suit claims the two "relished" the media attention after the videos of Belichick and Hudson became public and that the two "disclosed additional private information" about Belichick and Hudson.

Hudson has previously taken public issue with Torre, as he had reported in the spring of 2025 that North Carolina had "banned" Hudson from the team's facilities. The athletic department subsequently issued a statement saying that wasn't the case.

articles.title: Man Utd's transfer policy to blame for club's worst Premier League start and not Michael Carrick, says Paul Merson
articles.summary: Michael Carrick's future at Man Utd is in doubt with the club inside the Premier League relegation zone; Mauricio Pochettino would be open to talks with Man Utd if he was approached by club; Sky Sports' Paul Merson says he would be surprised if Carrick was sacked
articles.body:
Carrick's job is increasingly in doubt, with United sitting in the Premier League relegation zone after taking only eight points from their first 10 games, and Mauricio Pochettino is open to a discussion if approached.

One win in 11 games, 30 goals conceded in all competitions, the worst record of any team in the top-five European leagues and a club-worst start to a league season has ramped up the pressure on Carrick - but Merson feels he is not at fault.

"I just can't blame the manager. They change managers left, right and centre all the time and it's the same results," said Merson.

"It doesn't matter if you have Arsene Wenger, Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola or Jose Mourinho sitting on the bench. The mistakes they are making are down to the players.

"If they weren't running around for the manager, they'd have been ripped to shreds by Roma and Aston Villa and they didn't. They came back in both of those games. I'd be quite surprised if they let Carrick go at the moment

"They got it the wrong way around with their transfer policy. The first window they went for buying forwards. The next window, they started bringing in midfield players and now at the end of the season, they're probably going to go and buy defenders.

"They should have gone with defenders first. You can't build a house on a puddle. You've got to have a strong defence and they haven't done that.

"They've done it completely the wrong way around and it's come back to bite them.

"They've got to look at themselves upstairs and think that they got this horribly wrong, not Michael Carrick."

United States head coach Pochettino could be set to return to the Premier League for the first time since leaving Chelsea in May 2024.

"He's got experience, major experience. He's worked in the Premier League a lot of times," said Merson. "If they get rid of Michael Carrick, they're not bringing someone in who's going to take six months to get used to the Premier League. This man's a top, top manager.

"I don't think Carrick could go, but if they could get Pochettino for £7m, that's a cheap deal. He's a good manager, but I think Michael Carrick can be a very good manager. They've just done it the wrong way round in all the transfer windows.

"Man Utd are not one of the biggest teams anymore, but they've still got one of the biggest expectations in football and that is the problem. I think Man United are, and this is no disrespect, a mid-table team.

"We keep on talking about Man United of 15 years ago. When they had Wayne Rooney, Cristiano Ronaldo and top draw players. It's not the case anymore.

"They're into buying players in the market who are a flip of a coin. They might be good, or they might not, and that's not how you do it at Man United. With the financial rules now, it's going to be difficult for them to get anywhere near back to where they were 15, 20, and 25 years ago.

"It's a great club and a massive club, but the expectations of managing that type of club, and where you've got to finish in the league, are very, very high, and I think that's what sometimes puts managers off."

articles.title: Galardón especial para Ramón Navarro, fotoperiodista de MARCA, en los XVII Premios Blázquez
articles.standfirst: Nueva edición de los tradicionales reconocimientos del Sevilla a la Prensa
articles.summary: Nueva edición de los tradicionales reconocimientos del Sevilla a la Prensa
articles.body: El Sevilla celebró este martes una nueva edición de sus ya tradicionales premios periodísticos, una iniciativa que alcanza ya los 17 años de trayectoria en el caso del Premio José Antonio Blázquez y los 14 en el Ruesga Bono. Con ellos, la entidad nervionense quiere poner en valor el trabajo de periodistas y fotoperiodistas vinculados a la actualidad del club. El antepalco del Sánchez-Pizjuán fue el escenario de una ceremonia en la que hubo espacio para los reconocimientos profesionales, los recuerdos y también las emociones más personales. La gala comenzó con un recuerdo especial a Enrique García y Nacho Ansó, fallecidos durante los últimos meses. Posteriormente, llegó el turno de homenajear a los profesionales sevillanos que formaron parte de la cobertura del Mundial de 2026, conquistado por España el pasado mes de julio en Estados Unidos. La mención especial recayó en José Manuel Oliva (COPE), David Martínez (TVE), Silvia Verde (RNE), Alejandro Ruesga (El País), Fran Santiago (Getty) y Miguel Ángel Morenatti (Diario AS). Uno de los momentos más especiales de la jornada llegó con un reconocimiento que no figuraba en el programa inicial. El protagonista fue Ramón Navarro, fotoperiodista de MARCA y ganador del premio Ruesga Bono en 2017, a quien el Sevilla quiso rendir homenaje después de que haya superado un cáncer. El club preparó una sorpresa para Navarro, que fue llamado al escenario para recibir el premio especial Ruesga Bono. Durante la entrega se destacó su fortaleza y su capacidad para afrontar la enfermedad, poniendo el acento en el valor de la unión y el apoyo de quienes le han acompañado durante este difícil proceso. Visiblemente emocionado y sin esperarse el reconocimiento, el periodista agradeció el gesto y reconoció que no encontraba fácilmente las palabras. Con su habitual sentido del humor, explicó que había acudido directamente del campo, todavía con barro en las botas, y que había pasado por un momento complicado, aunque ya se encuentra bien. Navarro también quiso acordarse de sus compañeros de profesión y reivindicó su deseo de continuar trabajando. Después de tres décadas dedicado al periodismo, dejó claro que todavía le quedan años por delante y bromeó con que, aunque algunos pudieran pensar en su retirada, resulta complicado hacerlo rodeado de tanta gente que le aprecia.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany: Head coach back at Bayern Munich after collapse
articles.summary: Bayern Munich say head coach Vincent Kompany is "on the road to recovery" following his recent collapse and treatment in hospital.
articles.body:
Head coach Vincent Kompany has returned to Bayern Munich's training ground after collapsing at the end of last month.

The 40-year-old former Manchester City captain was taken to hospital after falling ill while watching the club's second team train.

Kompany was diagnosed with meningeal irritation - an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord.

Bayern said in a statement: "Vincent Kompany is on the road to recovery and has been back at the training ground since the start of the week."

However, the Bundesliga leaders did not hold a training session, with most players away on international duty.

English coach Aaron Danks has been in charge during Kompany's absence, leading Bayern to four victories and a draw.

They face Cologne next on 20 November after the end of the two-week international break.

articles.title: No hay ningún jugador más solidario que Lamine Yamal
articles.standfirst: El extremo culé es el futbolista que más asistencias proporciona en las grandes ligas
articles.summary: El extremo culé es el futbolista que más asistencias proporciona en las grandes ligas
articles.body: Los adjetivos calificativos aduladores ya se agotan para describir y nombrar el juego, la calidad y las aportaciones futbolísticas de Lamine Yamal. El extremo culé, que está en Barcelona descansando y se sumará en unos días a la selección española para participar en el encuentro contra Inglaterra del próximo domingo, no deja de asombrar al mundo con su talento. No se cansa de superar registros, a los rivales y a sí mismo. El joven atacante no sólo marca, asiste: es el futbolista más generoso de las grandes ligas: ninguno ha regalado tantos pases finales como él. Lamine Yamal lidera la clasificación de asistencias de LaLiga. Ha habilitado a sus compañeros para que marcasen en ocho ocasiones. Le siguen, con seis, Javi Hernández, del Espanyol, y su compañero y amigo Fermín López, con cinco. El canterano culé asistió a Cancelo y a Gabriel Jesús contra el Racing de Santander; a Raphinha, en su doblete contra el Sevilla; a Koundé, frente al Getafe; al exatacante del Arsenal otra vez en La Cartuja; y a Fermín López contra el Alavés y este pasado domingo en el Metropolitano frente a los de Simeone. Dio la primera asistencia en el choque contra el equipo cántabro, y desde entonces, en LaLiga, ha repetido éxito en seis de los últimos siete encuentros. Su acierto en el pase y capacidad de asociación se han visto incrementados, por lo tanto, en estas semanas más recientes. Pero Lamine Yamal tampoco tiene rival en esta faceta del juego en Europa. Ningún otro profesional de las grandes ligas continentales le supera. Así, el futbolista que más pases finales ha proporcionado en la Premier League es el alemán Pascal Grob, del Brighton, con seis; en la Bundesliga, Marco Grüll, extremo austríaco del Werder Bremen suma también ocho, como el culé; en la Serie A, Juan Miranda, del Bolonia, atesora seis; y en la Ligue 1, Florian Thauvin, del Lens, también le empata con 8. Las aportaciones de Lamine Yamal como asistente van incluso más allá de LaLiga, ya que también ha proporcionado cuatro en la Champions League: dos contra el Feyenoord y otras dos contra el Galatasaray. En total, por lo tanto, suma 12, una cifra que no ha alcanzado ningún otro jugador en este arranque de curso. El internacional no tiene rival en cuanto a habilitar a sus compañeros y en su capacidad de asociación y generosidad. Nico Paz, del Como de Cesc Fàbregas, suma un pase final más en la máxima competición continental, pero en total no le da caza, ya que el mediocentro sólo ha logrado tres en el torneo doméstico italiano. Lamine Yamal, que además ha marcado ¡13! goles (10 en LaLiga y tres en la Champions League), ya suma 40 asistencias en el torneo doméstico, con 19 años y 118 días. Según MisterChip, es el primer jugador en la historia en alcanzar esa cifra en la competición regular nacional antes de los 22. Otro récord más que uno de los capitanes culés, a pesar de su corta edad, acumula en su exitosa trayectoria.

articles.title: Raúl enseña su hoja de ruta en Oviedo: "Me gusta un equipo vertical, agresivo, que busque el gol"
articles.standfirst: El exentrenador del Castilla apuesta por la ambición y la flexibilidad táctica, descarta mirar al banquillo del Real Madrid y sitúa el ascenso como horizonte
articles.summary: El exentrenador del Castilla apuesta por la ambición y la flexibilidad táctica, descarta mirar al banquillo del Real Madrid y sitúa el ascenso como horizonte
articles.body: Raúl González Blanco no quiere que su Real Oviedo sea un equipo que espere a que sucedan las cosas. En su presentación como nuevo entrenador azul, celebrada en el Carlos Tartiere, dibujó el perfil futbolístico que pretende construir: "Me gusta un equipo vertical, agresivo, que busque el gol, que sepa defender". Es su primera declaración de principios en un banquillo profesional fuera de la estructura del Real Madrid, aunque dejó claro que no habrá recetas inamovibles. El técnico explicó que todavía está evaluando los perfiles y las dinámicas del vestuario. El calendario no concede tregua y el estreno ante el Girona concentra toda su atención. "Los partidos antes de Navidad nos darán mucha información, pero el del sábado es el más importante", afirmó. Su intención es aprovechar lo que ya funciona y añadir progresivamente los mecanismos que considera necesarios. No habrá un dibujo obligatorio. Preguntado por la posibilidad de jugar con tres defensas, recordó que en el Castilla había empleado diferentes estructuras. "Estoy abierto a todas las estructuras y quiero poner a los mejores", respondió. La elección dependerá de las características de la plantilla, del estado físico de los futbolistas y de cada contexto competitivo. El objetivo de fondo, sin embargo, sí quedó perfectamente definido. "Intentaremos estar bien posicionados y pelearemos por el objetivo, que tiene que ser estar en Primera división", proclamó. Raúl habló de una temporada larga, "un maratón con muchas batallas", en la que el equipo tendrá que competir cada jornada sin perder de vista la clasificación. La elección del Oviedo no fue casual. Después de un periodo sin entrenar, buscaba un club con historia, una ciudad entregada al fútbol y un proyecto que le generara confianza. Reconoció contactos con otras entidades, pero el papel de David Fernández, director deportivo azul, resultó decisivo. También valoró la estabilidad que percibe en la propiedad y el desarrollo de la ciudad deportiva. "Tengo mucha ilusión, creo que puedo aportar cosas", manifestó. Raúl habló con Jesús Martínez, presidente del Grupo Pachuca, y encontró afinidad en la manera de entender el fútbol. "Le gustan los equipos atrevidos, que juegan bien y atacan", explicó sobre el propietario, aunque introdujo un matiz esencial: "Esto es equilibrio, atacar y defender". La ambición ofensiva, por tanto, no estará reñida con la organización sin balón. El nombre del Real Madrid también apareció en la comparecencia. Ante la pregunta de si se imagina algún día entrenando al primer equipo blanco, evitó abrir una puerta al futuro: "Me veo estando aquí. Es donde me han dado la oportunidad y la confianza. Y estoy muy contento". El nuevo entrenador insistió en que afronta esta etapa con entusiasmo y con el deseo de disfrutar de su trabajo diario sobre el césped. En su primer contacto con el grupo, mantuvo una conversación con los capitanes y destacó la predisposición que encontró. Su experiencia como futbolista y capitán le ayuda, considera, a comprender las necesidades de un vestuario, aunque sabe que dirigir desde el banquillo exige adaptarse. También dedicó palabras de elogio a Enzo Pérez, ausente ante el Girona por su compromiso con la selección sub 19, al que describió como un futbolista de gran proyección. ¿Refuerzos en enero? Raúl no adelantó peticiones concretas. Prefiere estudiar la evolución del plantel antes de hablar de necesidades. "Tengo una buena plantilla, no me quejo; si vemos cosas mejorables, lo haremos", aseguró. Y resumió qué espera transmitir a la grada: "Que la gente disfrute, que vea un equipo que ha luchado con coraje, que no se rinde nunca".

articles.title: José Ignacio Navarro: "Tenemos que mantener este ritmo de puntos"
articles.standfirst: El director deportivo del Sevilla habló también de los delanteros y de la renovación de Castrín
articles.summary: El director deportivo del Sevilla habló también de los delanteros y de la renovación de Castrín
articles.body: El Sevilla ha cumplido un año más con su ya tradicional cita con el periodismo y el antepalco del Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán ha auspiciado este martes la entrega de los XVII Premios Blázquez y los XIV Premios de fotoperiodismo Ruesga Bono. Tras finalizar el acto, el director deportivo del Sevilla, José Ignacio Navarro, pasó por los micrófonos de 'Sólo el Sevilla', de los medios de comunicación del club. El directivo sevillano hizo balance de este primer tercio de LaLiga. La competición casera vuelve a parar por los compromisos de las selecciones, en este caso, después de 12 jornadas: "Llevamos casi un tercio y nos encontramos dentro del objetivo marcado, que era el de competir en todos los partidos, tanto en casa como fuera, sin que se escapen muchos puntos. Tenemos esa imagen de equipo conseguida, pero la evaluación será al final de la temporada. Ahora hay que mantener este ritmo de puntos e imagen de equipo mostrada, con suerte de evitar lesiones y trabajando para seguir en esta línea para conseguir los objetivos". Navarro, además, habló de los jugadores de ataque del equipo: "Una cosas son los goles y otra es el comportamiento ofensivo del equipo, y estamos contentos con eso, incluidos los delanteros. Isaac está marcando y a Lucas Stassin y Robbie Ure hay que darles ese punto de paciencia porque son los dos jugadores muy jóvenes y vienen de fuera. Lucas todavía es sub-21 y Robbie viene de Suecia, siendo convocado por primera vez por Escocia recientemente. Hay que reforzar su adaptación". El directivo sevillista, que admitió que "desde que el árbitro pitó el final del partido, que estábamos jodidos por el empate a cero con el Alavés, nos pusimos en modo derbi". "Es el siguiente partido y cada uno lo afrontamos como el último. Estamos en modo derbi desde hace varios días", añadió. Por último explicó en qué situación está el proceso de renovación de Andrés Castrín: "Nuestra intención es que sea jugador del Sevilla los próximos años, le hemos hecho diferentes propuestas a su agente, una oferta que entendemos que es competitiva, ajustada a la realidad deportiva y económica del Sevilla, y estamos esperando su respuesta".

articles.title: A qué hora es el Tavernes - Valencia: dónde ver, canal y dónde ver en TV hoy el partido de Copa del Rey
articles.standfirst: El conjunto de La Safor vive una noche histórica ante el Valencia en Mestalla tras el aplazamiento por el trágico accidente ferroviario de Urda
articles.summary: El conjunto de La Safor vive una noche histórica ante el Valencia en Mestalla tras el aplazamiento por el trágico accidente ferroviario de Urda
articles.body: El Tavernes y el Valencia se enfrentan este martes 10 de noviembre a las 21:00 horas en Mestalla en el partido correspondiente a la primera ronda de la Copa del Rey. El encuentro debía disputarse inicialmente el 28 de octubre, pero fue aplazado a raíz del trágico accidente ferroviario de Urda. La eliminatoria mantiene su carácter singular: aunque el Tavernes ejerce como equipo local, el duelo se juega en el estadio valencianista. La Federación Española de Fútbol autorizó en su día el traslado del partido a Mestalla tras la petición realizada por el club de La Safor. De este modo, el Valencia tendrá formalmente la condición de visitante pese a disputar el encuentro en su propio campo. La nueva fecha ha alterado las circunstancias con las que ambos equipos afrontan la eliminatoria. El Valencia llega después de caer en Mestalla ante el Real Madrid y mantiene una preocupante racha como local, ya que no ha ganado ninguno de los siete partidos de Liga disputados en su estadio esta temporada. Además, el aplazamiento provoca que Javier Aguirre no pueda contar con varios internacionales convocados por sus selecciones, entre ellos Stole Dimitrievski, Mouctar Diakhaby ni Aliou Dieng. El Tavernes, por su parte, afronta la cita con más descanso. El conjunto vallero no disputó este fin de semana su encuentro liguero frente al Rayo Ibense, programado para el domingo, que no tenía fechas alternativas para poder celebrarlo. Por este motivo, se aplazó el encuentro de Liga y ha podido preparar con más tiempo una eliminatoria histórica para la entidad. La cita supone uno de los partidos más importantes de la historia reciente del Tavernes. El conjunto de La Safor, campeón de la Nostra Copa y vencedor ante el Maracena en la ronda previa, milita en la Lliga Comunitat (sexta categoría del fútbol español) y tendrá la oportunidad de medirse a un rival de Primera División en un escenario como Mestalla. Para el partido se han vendido más de 20.000 entradas, y está previsto que se desplacen desde Tavernes más de 5.000 aficionados bien en viajes organizados en autocares o en coches particulares. El Tavernes - Valencia, correspondiente a la primera ronda de la Copa del Rey, se disputa este martes 10 de noviembre a las 21:00 horas en Mestalla, con el conjunto de La Safor como equipo local y el Valencia como visitante a efectos federativos. El encuentro podrá verse en directo a través de Movistar LALIGA, según la programación televisiva de MARCA. Toda la información previa y posterior del encuentro estará disponible también en MARCA.com, junto con el resultado y la actualidad de la jornada copera.

articles.title: Shea and Pierce Charles: Birthdays and broken lamps - at home with Northern Ireland brothers
articles.summary: Before Northern Ireland's Nations League matches, BBC Sport joins Shea and Pierce Charles at their London home to discuss birthdays, steak sandwiches and starring for Michael O'Neill's young team.
articles.body:
Pierce Charles can't help but smile as he waits for Shea to walk into the kitchen.

It's Shea's 23rd birthday and he has a cake to surprise him, something he knows will embarrass his older brother.

Right on cue, he gets the response that he was looking for as Shea has a sheepish smile, and Pierce launches into a rendition of 'Happy Birthday' for the cameras.

In an exclusive interview at their London home, the brothers talk about breaking lamps while playing football as kids, debating who does the chores and the upcoming release of video game Grand Theft Auto VI.

With a cup of tea offered and shoes off at the door, you wouldn't think you were chatting with two international footballers, especially two who are riding the crest of a wave on the pitch.

London traffic aside, they are enjoying life in the hustle and bustle of the city as they live in England's capital for the first time.

"It's better than I thought it was going to be, I didn't think I was going to enjoy it," said Pierce who is spending the season on loan at Queens Park Rangers from Manchester City.

"I actually love it, and living together has been good. There's so much to do in London," added midfielder Shea, who joined Fulham from Southampton in a £30m move in August.

Using international football to reignite Premier League dreams

NI win in Georgia after Kvaratskhelia penalty miss

It is the first time the brothers have lived in London, but the third time they have lived together.

Having been born and grown up in Manchester, they came through Manchester City's academy before Pierce joined Sheffield Wednesday aged 16.

Shea stayed at the Etihad and made his Premier League debut under Pep Guardiola in May 2023 before signing for Southampton that summer.

The brothers were reunited at Wednesday when Shea joined on loan for the 2024-25 campaign, but there was some 200 miles between them last year as the midfielder returned to St Mary's.

This summer, after impressive performances for Wednesday and Northern Ireland, Pierce returned to Manchester City in a long-term deal before joining QPR on loan.

Not to be outdone, Shea earned a switch back to the Premier League with Fulham as he became Northern Ireland's first £30m footballer.

Both based in west London, that gave them the opportunity to move back in together, reigniting debates over who is better at the Grand Theft Auto games and Fortnite and who cooks the better steak sandwich.

They both want to claim top honours, but Pierce feels he will have the edge if he can get the peppercorn sauce recipe off the chef at QPR.

Older brother Eoin and parents Mary and Kelvin often come to visit, too, and there's more debate over who makes the house presentable, and whether doing the dishwasher actually counts as a chore.

"I think she secretly wants it to be messy, so she can have a little dig at us and do it anyway," jokes Pierce about Mary, who was born in Northern Ireland.

"She enjoys it really, she's not on holiday," Shea laughs.

Quickly realising the danger of getting a telling off on her next visit, Shea adds, "Mum is class. We appreciate mum".

Before the brothers sit down for a chat, there's time for a kick about in the garden for a game of 'two touch'.

It doesn't take long for their competitive side to shine through, and a best of three quickly becomes best of five then, eventually, a rematch.

Conversation turns to memories of similar games in the family garden as kids and how things used to always take a similarly competitive turn.

"When we used to play Wembley I would have always beaten you two and the loser went in nets," said Shea.

"If you want a fun fact, people might think he is the best player now but Shea was actually the worst out of us when we were younger in the back garden," Pierce was quick to respond.

"It was me, then Eoin and then Shea. To be fair, he's improved massively since."

There's a blame game over a broken clock and lamp, and middle child Shea has to plead his innocence over the latter.

"I broke the clock but I didn't break the lamp. It actually wasn't me, I swear," recalled Shea, still pleading his case before a mischievous "I loved that lamp" almost makes him look guilty.

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC Two NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website

The brothers have yet to hit London's tourist spots since moving to the capital, but a trip to Thorpe Park just outside the city is on the cards.

Their first memories of London are from visiting their cousins growing up, and there have been trips to Wembley to see childhood club Manchester City.

But the London 2012 Olympics stand out as an early memory, when the brothers would have been eight and nine years of age.

They remember meeting Team GB heptathlete Katarina Johnson-Thompson and recall racing outside of the London Stadium.

"There were little events on outside the stadium," Shea recalled.

"Like the 50 metres and that sort of stuff. I won my race."

Now the home of West Ham United, both brothers have played at the ground this season, some 14 years on from watching the Olympics at the same venue.

When QPR visited West Ham in October, Pierce was the hero as he saved Jarrod Bowen's last-gasp penalty to deny the Hammers three points.

His man of the match trophy from that game is proudly displayed in their home.

"It looks so much different from what I remember," said Shea on the London Stadium.

"And then we're playing in it 14 years later," added Pierce.

"It's mad, we're getting on a bit aren't we?"

The Charles brothers are just two players in a young and exciting Northern Ireland squad.

Michael O'Neill's side currently top Group B2 in the Nations League after four matches, and they have yet to concede a goal.

The campaign started in Georgia in September and both Shea and Pierce played their part in a famous win.

Pierce saved a penalty from Paris Saint-Germain star Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, and also made another big intervention to deny Georges Mikautadze.

Then, nine minutes into additional time, Shea popped up with a late winner to kick-start a window that would see Northern Ireland top their Nations League group after four matches, without conceding a goal.

"I think that's what started the good run," said Pierce.

"You can't win a game like that and fall off."

Now, Northern Ireland will look to finish the job as they host Ukraine in Belfast on Saturday, and finish the campaign in Hungary on 17 November.

"Two wins would be the dream and it would set us up nicely for the next few years," said Pierce.

"The next few games will be tough but we can't wait."

Given they live together and will be in Northern Ireland camp side-by-side - do they get sick of each other?

"It feels like I can't get away from you when we're on camp, but at least it's not shared rooms," said Shea.

"We're just joined at the hip," said Pierce, who added he doesn't get fed up with spending time with his brother.

"We're always together but we're not always together, if you know what I mean."

articles.title: Jimbo Fisher Reportedly 'Pushing Hard' for FSU HC Job, New Rumors on Search to Replace Mike Norvell
articles.summary: Jimbo Fisher is doing his part to make a reunion with Florida State happen.
articles.body:
Jimbo Fisher is doing his part to make a reunion with Florida State happen.

USA Today 's John Brice reported Tuesday that Fisher "is pushing hard for the job and calling potential staffers, and Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann."

Granted, Brice spoke to one college executive who cautioned against extrapolating anything from the rumors about the FSU job. The school is only a day removed from officially naming Jeff Purinton as the new athletic director.

"Anyone telling you much has happened at Florida State in their coaching search is full of it," the college exec said. "They just hired Purinton as AD. Nothing of consequence has happened yet."

Even before the Seminoles fired Mike Norvell, Fisher was linked with a shocking return to Tallahassee. He posted a .783 winning percentage in eight years at the school and delivered its most recent national title in 2013.

FSU hasn't enjoyed the same kind of consistency after Fisher exited for the Texas A&M job, so it's understandable why some fans and boosters might want him back.

But Fisher left the program in a st a te of disarray , which played a role in the Seminoles' broad downturn.

The 61-year-old was also a flop with the Aggies. They paid him a record-setting buyout of almost $77 million, which was a sign of how bad things had gotten in College Station.

Coaches are no different from athletes in that they can have a peak and decline phase.

Excluding the pandemic-shortened 2020 season, 2014 is the last time one of Fisher's teams finished in the top five of the Associated Press Top 25 poll. In addition, it's not a complete coincidence that his intricate pro-style offense delivered diminishing returns at the same time the transfer portal caused more roster turnover than over.

Coaching hires can be a complete crapshoot. Candidates who seemingly check off every box and prove to be a major disappointment. That applied to Fisher and his A&M run.

Florida State could nonetheless see Fisher as a relatively safe choice given his overall track record, specifically his previous experience with the Seminoles.

articles.summary: El delantero del Real Madrid se cae de la lista de España por una microrrotura en el psoas y Guillermo Trujillano será su sustituto
articles.body: Enzo Alves no estará en el Mundial sub-17 de Catar. El delantero arrastra una lesión muscular desde su último partido con el conjunto blanco y esta ha provocado que finalmente haya sido desconvocado para la cita mundialista. En su lugar acudirá Guillermo Trujillano, canterano del Atlético de Madrid. Tal y como adelantó MARCA el pasado domingo, el atacante sufrió una microrrotura en el psoas durante la primera parte del partido que enfrentó al juvenil madridista con el Rayo Vallecano. Las primeras pruebas apuntaban a una baja de alrededor de dos semanas, un plazo demasiado ajustado para el estreno de España, previsto frente a China el próximo día 20. El seleccionador David Cubillo había apostado por Enzo Alves y Yeremaiah como únicos delanteros de la convocatoria, pero el segundo —también futbolista del Real Madrid— llega entre algodones tras más de un mes de baja. Se espera que esté disponible para el inicio del torneo, aunque mantener a dos nueves en el aire era un riesgo excesivo de cara a la fase de grupos, a pesar de que otros jugadores de ataque, como Roberto Tomás, pudiesen actuar de ‘9’.

articles.title: De Jong: "Estoy en forma, feliz y muy motivado, las lesiones te dan más ganas de volver a jugar al fútbol"
articles.standfirst: Valora su estado y su rol con Países Bajos
articles.summary: Valora su estado y su rol con Países Bajos
articles.body: Frenkie de Jong ya está concentrado con la selección de Países Bajos que dirige Xavi Hernández. El centrocampista neerlandés, que ha reconocido que su cambio de ubicación (de central y lateral) en los últimos encuentros no tendrá mucha continuidad, se mostró ilusionado por su recuperación tras la lesión (durante el Mundial padeció una rotura del ligamento lateral interno de la rodilla derecha) y ante la posibilidad de ser capitán de su combinado nacional ante la baja por causa médica de Virgil van Dijk. El profesional culé también se refirió al estilo de juego del extécnico azulgrana. Recuperación tras lesión "Estoy en forma, feliz y muy motivado. No creo que se aprenda nada de las lesiones, pero sí que te dan más ganas de volver a jugar al fútbol". Capitán "Depende del entrenador anunciarlo, pero sin duda es posible. No soy muy hablador. Siempre se oye a Virgil por encima de los demás, él es nuestro verdadero líder, también verbalmente. Cuando llevo el brazalete, puedo servir de ejemplo a los demás por mi comportamiento y profesionalidad". Discreto "También viví la experiencia de tener a Messi como capitán. Nunca levantaba la voz y era el jefe indiscutible. Digamos que, con el brazalete, me situaría en algún punto entre Messi y Virgil. Sería un gran honor si llegara a suceder esta semana". Xavi "Es muy claro en su planteamiento y en lo que quiere ver. Durante el primer parón internacional ya observé algunos patrones en la construcción del juego que son característicos de él. El hecho de que también fuera centrocampista me resulta especialmente agradable". Jugar con Joey Veerman "Estoy de acuerdo con el entrenador en que los buenos futbolistas siempre pueden jugar juntos. Joey es tácticamente sólido, técnicamente bueno y tiene una gran visión de juego. Hay muchos centrocampistas en la selección con los que puedo jugar".

articles.title: Scott McTominay: Scotland midfielder had heart 'shocked' two days before World Cup opener against Haiti
articles.summary: The 29-year-old missed Sebastien Pocognoli's first camp as he recovered from heart surgery; Scotland host North Macedonia on November 13, with their final Nations League game away to Switzerland three days later
articles.body:
The Napoli midfielder underwent a cardiac ablation procedure in Manchester in September to treat a mild, benign heart arrhythmia that first came to light after the Scots arrived in the United States in early June and then continued to affect him in August while back in Italy playing for his club.

At the time, the Scotland camp, clearly keen to keep McTominay's situation under wraps, said the 29-year-old had missed training in the lead-up to the World Cup due to a stomach complaint.

But, speaking at a press conference at Hampden on Tuesday, the former Manchester United player said: "I had to go and get the shock on my heart two days before the Haiti game."

McTominay played all three of Scotland's matches at the World Cup but struggled to hit the heights as his team exited at the group stage.

"I was 100 per cent (fit), but obviously when you're sat in a hospital bed two days before the first game of the World Cup about to get put to sleep, it's not ideal, is it?" he said.

"You've prepared so well, I was in such good condition and then something like that happens and you're thinking, 'How is this happening to me?'

"It's nowhere near an excuse, but it's something that you have to look back on and say, 'Well, it's part of the process'.

"Obviously, with the way the World Cup went, it was at least two, three weeks of me sitting there disappointed, not quite with it mentally. I needed time to settle down and have a break.

"After the World Cup, it was probably the most disappointed I've ever been in my career.

"I'm always one for a glass half full, but that one took a good couple of weeks to get out of my system."

McTominay returned to action with Napoli at the start of this season, but after playing their first two Serie A matches, he decided surgery was the only option and duly spent all of September on the sidelines after undergoing a corrective procedure.

That meant he missed Scotland's first four matches under new boss Sebastien Pocognoli, but he is now back with the national team for this month's Nations League double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland after featuring in all nine of his club's matches since the last international break.

"I'm good. I'm feeling much, much better than what I was," he said. "I feel like it was something that needed to be done. In your career you have moments like that where things can take you a bit by surprise.

"Obviously, it looks a lot worse to people in the media and family and friends who reach out to you after they've seen news relating to a heart issue. But it was a relatively straightforward procedure which went really, really well in Manchester.

"I'm just really happy to be back playing football again. That's the most important thing in my life and it always will be."

articles.title: Manchester United reportedly eyeing Mauricio Pochettino, but USMNT players remain unfazed
articles.summary: Pochettino is once again being linked to a major European club job. But with Manchester United reportedly interested, USMNT players say the speculation hasn'...
articles.body:
FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. — U.S. players and officials have grown accustomed to breathless bulletins about their famous coach, Mauricio Pochettino, being linked with major club jobs in Europe.

His name surfaced with Tottenham Hotspur in 2025, AC Milan this year and other openings overseas since he joined the U.S. two years ago. It's business as usual in the soccer world, where fickle clubs with high expectations swap coaches at any sign of trouble.

Now, amid Manchester United's woeful start this season, Pochettino is reportedly being targeted to return to England , where he made his mark with Tottenham and later guided Chelsea. (He has also led Paris Saint-Germain, among others.)

United is one of the most prestigious brands in not just soccer but all of sports, and with Michael Carrick on the searing-hot seat as the Red Devils sit in the relegation zone, the spotlight has apparently turned to Pochettino as a potential successor.

In other words, if Manchester United is talking, Pochettino owes it to himself to listen.

He greeted reporters and guests from a distance before training Tuesday but did not comment. U.S. Soccer Federation president Cindy Parlow Cone did not comment on ESPN's report and spoke casually about U.S. teams.

Both she and USSF chief operating officer Dan Helfrich engaged with Pochettino in light conversation on the field before he joined the players and staff. Cone and Helfrich are often at the national training center near Atlanta, and their visit Tuesday was preplanned.

Two days into workouts, the U.S. delegation continues regular preparations for the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti. The first leg is Saturday in Miami, the second next Tuesday in Cincinnati.

Before Tuesday's practice, veteran left back Antonee Robinson and 17-year-old forward Cavan Sullivan addressed the Pochettino reports.

"That news kind of got sprung on us like the rest of the world," said Robinson, who plays for Fulham in the Premier League. "Similar things happened in the past, after the World Cup, where huge teams lose their manager and they start looking at possible candidates. For us to have a manager who's linked with those sorts of jobs means we're very lucky we're working with a top-level manager."

Robinson added that such news "never seems to leak into the work we do, whether it's the World Cup or whether it's going to be this camp."

Robinson called it "outside noise" and "he's very much focused on getting the best out of the team."

Pochettino, 54, re-signed with the U.S. after the summer's World Cup, inking a deal through the 2030 tournament. Any suitor would need to pay a multimillion-dollar buyout fee to the USSF.

There is no perfect time for a coaching change, but the beginning of a World Cup cycle is the best-case scenario. That would afford the U.S. replacement to forge bonds and implement plans before major competitions in the coming years.

A coach change, though, close to a World Cup is problematic — and the USSF has experienced just that. Jurgen Klinsmann's failed second term after the 2014 World Cup left Bruce Arena with less than a year to get things back on track. The U.S. failed to qualify for the 2018 tournament, ending a streak of seven consecutive appearances.

Gregg Berhalter's second stint after the 2022 World Cup came to an end following the 2024 Copa America disappointment. Pochettino then had about a year to instill a fresh culture and identify players and another six months to prepare for the World Cup on home soil last summer. Aiming for the quarterfinals, the Americans won their group but once again were ousted in the Round of 16.

The USSF's hope is that a full term under Pochettino would put the team on course to make a breakthrough at the 2030 World Cup, which will take place on three continents. His introduction of young talent, such as Sullivan and several other teenagers, has laid the groundwork for long-term success.

The Manchester United news has not caused distractions, Robinson said.

"As soccer players, we are pretty used to sort of fast-changing environments and games coming pretty fast," he said. "So we're all very good at just focusing on the next task at hand, whether that's the next session or the next game coming up. I don't really look at … 'Oh, this could be the last time he's in front of me.' It's just focusing on we've got a game on the weekend."

Sullivan spoke highly of Pochettino, who invited him to his first senior camp earlier this fall for four friendlies. The Philadelphia Union star became the youngest goal scorer in program history.

"He's taken me under his wing in the most tremendous way possible," he said. "I was obviously a young guy coming in, and he told me to just play free and be myself, have confidence in my ability. That didn't mean the standard was lower for me. That standard remained the same for everybody in the camp and every training and every game. I'm someone who really appreciates that – the directness on the field, but also the warmth, the hugs."

articles.title: Greg Schiano Reportedly Returning to Rutgers for 2027 CFB Season Despite 2-7 Record
articles.summary: Despite its 2-7 record this season, Rutgers reportedly won't be making the change many had anticipated when the year is over.
articles.body:
Despite its 2-7 record this season, Rutgers reportedly won't be making the change many had anticipated when the year is over.

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Scarlet Knights head coach Greg Schiano will return for the 2027 season, which will mark his 19th year with the program over two stints.

Thamel added that Schiano recently met with Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn "to lay out a plan for improvement next year." He's under contract through the 2029 season, and he would've been owed $18.6 million if he had been fired.

Still, Schiano's return is a bit of a surprise after comments from Zinn recently surfaced, indicating that he was on the hot seat.

"If we are investing in your roster, in facilities, in operations, in salaries at ninth in the league, you should perform at ninth in the league. And if you're above that -- fantastic, that's awesome. Keep going, how do we get in an even better spot? But if all of those things put you ninth in the league and you're performing 14th, there's a problem there," Zinn told sports marketing firm Navigate , referencing the Scarlet Knights tying for 14th in the Big Ten last season. "Something is not working, and you've got to be able to get close to that point, show a trajectory to there or unfortunately that's probably not going to end well."

Since returning to Rutgers in 2020, Schiano has achieved just two winning seasons, going 7-6 in 2023 and 2024. The Scarlet Knights lost two of their three bowl game appearances over that span, and they likely won't be selected for a bowl game for the second straight year after securing back-to-back losing seasons.

After saving his job, Schiano will focus on trying to help Rutgers end its three-game skid on Saturday against Nebraska (5-4).

articles.title: Next Man Utd manager: What are club's managerial options amid doubts over Michael Carrick's future
articles.summary: As doubts grow over Manchester United boss Michael Carrick's future, what are the club's managerial options?
articles.body:
With one victory in their first 10 Premier League matches, Manchester United have made their worst start to a top-flight campaign since the 1986-87 season.

They are 18th in the table, one point above bottom club Crystal Palace .

United directors will meet in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Michael Carrick's future as his 10-month spell as head coach comes under major scrutiny.

If the 45-year-old former player departs, it would mean an eighth permanent boss for the Red Devils since Sir Alex Ferguson retired 13 years ago.

That would be as many managerial changes as they have made across the previous 68 years dating back to Sir Matt Busby's appointment in 1945.

BBC Sport takes a look at the leading candidates who could replace Carrick.

Major trophies won: 1 Ligue 1, 1 French Cup

Premier League record: P294, W150; Win percentage: 51; Points per game ratio (PPG): 1.77

Did you know: Pochettino averaged 1.89 points per game during his spell at Tottenham , the best ratio of any Spurs manager to have taken charge of 25 or more Premier League games.

United's long-standing interest in the Argentine, 54, dates back a decade.

At Spurs , he moulded their best team in a generation, but ultimately came up short of winning a trophy, losing both the Champions League and League Cup finals, and posted second and third-placed finishes. Silverware did come at Paris St-Germain with a league title, but a spell at Chelsea proved tougher with a League Cup final defeat by Liverpool in 2024.

Having led the USA to the last 16 of the World Cup on home soil he signed a new contract taking him up to the 2030 tournament. Pochettino has an exciting group of young players to work with for the national team - led by Manchester City -bound 17-year-old Cavan Sullivan - but he has always made it clear he has unfinished business in the Premier League.

A reported buyout clause in Pochettino's contract is worth $10million (£7.44m), while it is also understood to contain clauses that would allow him to leave for specific high-profile jobs.

Carrick's Man Utd future to be decided at Wednesday meeting

What Howe could bring to Man Utd - and what are the challenges?

Did you know: Only Hansi Flick (88.9%) has a better win percentage by a Bayern Munich manager in the Champions League than Nagelsmann's 83.3%.

Nagelsmann first impressed with his work at Hoffenheim, where he became the youngest head coach in Bundesliga history aged 28, leading them from relegation struggles to the Champions League.

He followed that by taking RB Leipzig to a Champions League semi-final in 2020 and Bayern Munich understandably came calling.

But despite winning the Bundesliga title in his first season he reportedly fell out with key players and did not survive a full second season.

In 2023, Nagelsmann took charge of a Germany side in transition, and they were narrowly beaten in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 by eventual winners Spain, but stepped down in the summer after Die Mannschaft were humbled by Paraguay in the World Cup last 32.

Still only 39, his reputation may have taken a bit of a hit, but the German is still regarded as one of Europe's best coaches. Manchester United 's director of recruitment Christopher Vivell also knows him well, having worked together at RB Leipzig.

Premier League record: P369 W140; Win percentage: 37.9; PPG: 1.36

Did you know: Eddie Howe (five) is one of only three managers with five or more wins against Mikel Arteta in all competitions, along with Pep Guardiola (11) and Jurgen Klopp (six).

His body of work in English football needs little introduction having led Bournemouth to the top flight for the first time in their history, before he confirmed his place in Newcastle folklore with their first major domestic trophy since lifting the FA Cup in 1955.

The League Cup final triumph over Liverpool was one of the greatest days in the club's history, while he also secured two top-five finishes to take the club back into the Champions League for the first time in 20 years.

Howe, 48, left in the summer after an underwhelming 12th-placed finish last term and Newcastle would only be due a a relatively small amount of compensation should he be tempted by the Old Trafford job.

Major trophies won: 5 Serie A, 1 Premier League, 1 FA Cup

Premier League record: P132, W83; Win percentage: 62.9; PPG: 2.03

Did you know: Chelsea won 30 of their 38 Premier League matches as they claimed the title in Antonio Conte's first season in charge in 2016-17.

A serial winner, Conte's managerial credentials are not in doubt.

He left Napoli of his own accord this summer just 12 months after delivering only the fourth top-flight title in their history.

That added to Serie A triumphs at Juventus (three) and Inter Milan, and spells at Chelsea and Tottenham .

Conte, 57, would appear to be a no-brainer of a choice to take over at United, but could the Italian's fiery nature and history of falling out with clubs count against him?

His last stint in English football ended under a cloud of controversy as he left Tottenham in 2023 following criticism of the players and the club's culture.

While he had success at Chelsea , Conte also reportedly clashed with both players and the board.

Major trophies won: 5 Europa League, 1 Ligue 1, 2 French Cups, 2 French League Cups

Premier League record: P200, W101; Win percentage: 50.5; PPG: 1.75

Did you know: Unai Emery has the best Premier League win percentage (51%) and points per game ratio (1.75) of any permanent Aston Villa boss.

Vastly experienced, the Spaniard's stock is at an all-time high courtesy of the superb job he has done since taking over at Villa in October 2022.

Having taken the club into the European Cup/Champions League for the first time for 41 years, the 55-year-old then ended their 30-year wait for silverware with success in last season's Europa League.

Despite having lost the spine of his team over the summer, Emery's new-look side are finding their feet again and the chances of him leaving for United look even slimmer with recent news he is expected to sign a new contract.

Premier League record: P29, W14; Win percentage: 48.3; PPG: 1.76

Did you know: After his initial appointment as United's interim boss in January, Michael Carrick had the most wins (12) and points (39) of any Premier League manager during the rest of the 2025-26 season.

Still clinging on to his job in the Old Trafford hot seat, could United's hierarchy actually decide to keep faith with Carrick?

After such a brilliant start and end to the season following his arrival in January, the wheels have come off spectacularly this term with only three wins from 15 matches in all competitions.

His team have at least shown fight with comebacks in recent games to beat Roma and salvage a point in a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa , but their overall stats are damning and the outlook doesn't look good for the 45-year-old, who won five Premier League titles and the Champions League as a United player.

The club are in the relegation zone and 18th is their lowest position after 10 games of a season for 40 years. It is also only the second time they have gone eight Premier League games without a victory.

articles.title: La dura vida del 9 puro en la selección
articles.standfirst: Samu, Borja Iglesias y Roberto, a cero los tres, no encuentran el camino que sí explotó Joselu
articles.summary: Samu, Borja Iglesias y Roberto, a cero los tres, no encuentran el camino que sí explotó Joselu
articles.body: Hace mucho que el puesto de delantero centro de la selección española es una posición desagradable para los arietes del estilo más clásico, los 9 de toda la vida. En la Eurocopa de 2012, a la que España acudió sin el mejor goleador de su historia, David Villa, lesionado, Del Bosque exploró, con Cesc, la vía de lo que se llamó el falso 9. La España de hoy, la que luce en su camiseta los parches de campeona de Europa y del mundo, es un equipo que funciona con precisión y en el que el puesto de delantero centro lo comparten dos goleadores alejados del perfil de 9 puro: Oyarzabal y Ferran. La naturaleza de la selección española se ha convertido en un ecosistema complicado para los delanteros que viven en el área rival. Desde que España ganó la Eurocopa, el 12 de julio de 2024, ha jugado 32 partidos y ha marcado 79 goles. De ellos, solo dos han llegado a través de delanteros centros clásicos. Joselu, en el 1-4 de Ginebra de septiembre de 2024, y Morata, en el 3-0 a Serbia de un mes más tarde, son los últimos jugadores con perfil de ariete puro que han marcado para España. En ese tiempo, la selección ha encontrado un delantero de época. De esos 79 goles desde la Euro, Oyarzabal suma 19, casi un cuarto del total (24%). A su espalda aparece Ferran, un extremo transfigurado en delantero. Y detrás de ellos, la sombra de Mikel Merino como recurso de urgencia. En ese tiempo, De la Fuente ha contado con tres arietes clásicos en sus planes, sin contar los minutos de Gonzalo ante Irak como jugador de apoyo antes del Mundial. Ninguno de ellos ha sido capaz de marcar. Es más, ninguno ha podido escapar a la sospecha de que para futbolistas de sus características es complicado brillar en esta selección. El primero fue Samu Aghehowa: cuatro partidos y 131 minutos de sequía. Al Mundial fue Borja Iglesias. Debutante con Luis Enrique, su recorrido con España refleja nueve partidos y 235 minutos. Y en la pasada ventana se estrenó Roberto Fernández: 90 minutos ante la República Checa con un solo remate a puerta.

articles.title: Women's Champions League: What is the prize money?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team break down the prize money on offer in the Women's Champions League.
articles.body:
The total prize pot available for clubs participating in the 2026-27 Women's Champions League proper is €18.2m (£15.2m), with €7.7m (£6.4m) on offer for participation in the qualifying rounds.

Uefa will also pay out €5.6m (£4.7m) to teams in the Women's Europa Cup, and a further €6.2m (£5.2m) in 'solidarity payments' to national associations that have at least one club participating in the Champions League.

The €18.2m Champions League prize pot has been in place since 2025, and will increase to €24.1m from 2027 to 2030.

How is Champions League money distributed?

Before any games are played, a guaranteed participation fee of €505,000 (£422,500) is paid to all 18 clubs that qualified for the league phase, with 75% paid as a down payment.

Performance-based money is then allocated as follows:

Final league phase ranking bonus: €10,000 (£8,200) per place (eg €10,000 for 18th, €180,000 for first)

Knockout phase play-offs: €100,000 (£83,700)

The knockout play-off, quarter and semi-final payments are given to both clubs participating.

The 'solidarity payments' are then made to clubs in top domestic women's leagues that did not take part in the Champions League proper.

These payments vary depending on the performance of the national association's club or clubs that took part in the Champions League.

Uefa state that the national associations must distribute their solidarity payments equally among clubs in their top domestic women's championship that did not qualify for the tournament, including those knocked out in qualifying and those taking part in the Europa Cup.

The rules also state these payments must be "earmarked for development purposes and may not be used for the fixed and ordinary costs of the club".

Uefa has also announced that the first €2m (£1.7m) of any surplus amounts (once sales are finalised) will be split between clubs participating in the league phase, with the remainder divided between league phase, qualifying and Euorpa clubs as well as solidarity payments.
