articles.title: Bellingham y la lección de Mourinho sobre sus medias: “Chaval, tienes nueve años, no tienes gemelos”
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista del Madrid se sincera en British Vogue, donde relata una anécdota con su entrenador y habla de su vida en Madrid, del Mundial y del estrés que le llegó a “consumir”
articles.summary: El centrocampista del Madrid se sincera en British Vogue, donde relata una anécdota con su entrenador y habla de su vida en Madrid, del Mundial y del estrés que le llegó a “consumir”
articles.body: Jude Bellingham ha concedido su primera gran entrevista para una revista de moda, la portada del número de diciembre de British Vogue, y en ella ha dejado varios pasajes de interés futbolístico y, sobre todo, madridista. El inglés habla de su entrenador en el Real Madrid, José Mourinho; de su vida en Madrid; de su esfuerzo por aprender castellano; del Mundial de 2026 con Inglaterra, y admite que la tensión de la pasada campaña llegó a “consumirle”. Bellingham relata una conversación reciente con el técnico portugués que, dice, se le ha quedado grabada. “Cuando entrenaba al Roma hace unos años, un niño en un entrenamiento se había cortado tres agujeros en la parte de atrás de los calcetines”, cuenta el jugador. “Mourinho fue hacia él y le dijo: ‘¿Por qué haces eso?’, y el chaval respondió: ‘Lo hace Bellingham, sirve para aliviar la presión en el gemelo’. Y Mourinho le soltó: ‘Chaval, tienes nueve años. No tienes gemelos’”. El gesto de los calcetines agujereados se ha convertido en una de las señas del centrocampista. Preguntado por lo que más le gusta de la ciudad, Bellingham no duda: “Jugar en el Real Madrid”. El inglés asegura que disfruta de la capital y de “sus muchos colores”, y describe incluso su relación con el clima: “Aunque llueva en Madrid, es un poco más, no sé… ¿elegante?”. El jugador reconoce que su día a día exige planificación por la exposición pública. Para algo tan sencillo como tomar un café, admite que suele buscar sitios a las afueras: “Siempre te van a reconocer, pero estás un poco más seguro en cuanto a que no te agobien”. Aun así, dice esforzarse por atender a los aficionados, especialmente a los niños: “Si pueden hacerse una foto contigo, van a estar encantados durante un buen rato y, en realidad, son cinco segundos de tu tiempo”. Bellingham cuenta que, al llegar a Madrid en 2023, estuvo cinco meses tomando clases de español, decidido a no quedarse en el “hola” y “gracias”. “Creo que una gran parte es tener la confianza suficiente para lanzarte a hablar”, explica. “Sabes que vas a equivocarte, y probablemente no vas a sonar exactamente bien, pero si la gente entiende lo que quieres decir, seguramente pensará: ‘Bien por intentarlo’”. El inglés describe la Copa del Mundo, en la que Inglaterra acabó tercera —su mejor resultado desde el título de 1966—, como “probablemente la mejor experiencia que he tenido en mi vida, y punto”. “El fútbol fue increíble, pero también estar en Estados Unidos y ver a los aficionados ingleses viajar hasta allí, cantando el ‘Wonderwall’…”, recuerda. Bellingham, que marcó los dos goles ante la Noruega de su excompañero Haaland en cuartos, admite que afrontó el torneo con una idea clara: “Mientras estaba dentro, tomé la decisión consciente de disfrutar esto. No pasa muy a menudo. Es raro”. Uno de los pasajes más personales en clave de rendimiento es el que dedica a la gestión de la presión. “Sentí que, por momentos la temporada pasada, me estaba consumiendo y me ponía muy tenso y estresado”, confiesa. El jugador explica que decidió buscar ayuda: “Empecé a hablar con alguien que me ayudó mucho con eso y con cómo manejar ese tipo de cosas”. Admite que sigue costándole desconectar del fútbol: “Es cuando llego a casa y he tenido cuatro partidos en 14 días; lo único que quiero es hacer mi recuperación el tiempo suficiente para, cuando termine, meterme en la cama”. Bellingham desvela también el apoyo que recibió de David Beckham, otra estrella inglesa que pasó por el Real Madrid, durante la Eurocopa de 2024, cuando las primeras actuaciones de Inglaterra fueron criticadas y surgieron rumores sobre el vestuario. “A veces no es el mensaje, sino el mensajero lo que lo hace más valioso”, afirma sobre las palabras del exjugador. “Tienes a alguien de tu lado que sabe de qué va esto”. En Vogue resume su relación con la exposición con una frase: “Fuera del campo, quiero ser un caballero”.

articles.title: Los jueces piden a Santi Mina que prepare su entrada en prisión
articles.standfirst: El ex jugador de Celta y Valencia fue declarado culpable por un delito de abuso sexual
articles.summary: El ex jugador de Celta y Valencia fue declarado culpable por un delito de abuso sexual
articles.body: La Sección Tercera de la Audiencia de Almería ha requerido a la defensa del futbolista Santi Mina que en el plazo de diez días presente sus alegaciones sobre la ejecución de la pena de cuatro años de cárcel por un delito de abuso sexual ocurrido en 2017 y declarada firme por el Tribunal Supremo. Según consta en el auto dictado por el tribunal almeriense, los magistrados otorgan a la representación procesal del condenado este margen para que "efectúe en un mismo escrito" las alegaciones relativas a la ejecución de su castigo. Al superar la condena los dos años de prisión, la suspensión ordinaria resulta inviable, por lo que el siguiente paso judicial, una vez consumido este trámite, será dictar un mandamiento para el ingreso voluntario del jugador en el centro penitenciario que elija. La Audiencia de Almería exige al futbolista gallego que se pronuncie sobre el cumplimiento de la "prohibición de aproximación a menos de 500 metros de la víctima y de comunicarse con él por cualquier medio, durante un período de doce años". Apercibe además a Santi Mina y le advierte de que puede "incurrir en delito de quebrantamiento de condena en caso de incumplimiento" de estas restricciones. El auto da igualmente traslado a la acusación particular para que se posicione sobre la forma de abono de la responsabilidad civil de 25.000 euros impuesta al jugador en concepto de daño moral. Asimismo, la resolución judicial declara firme la sentencia absolutoria dictada respecto al también futbolista David Goldar. Este proceso de ejecución se abre después de que la Sala de lo Penal del Tribunal Supremo ratificara el pasado septiembre la condena a Mina por abusar sexualmente de una mujer en la madrugada del 16 de junio de 2017 en una furgoneta estacionada en las proximidades de una discoteca de Mojácar (Almería). El Alto Tribunal desestimó íntegramente los veintinueve motivos del recurso de casación de la defensa y señaló que el acusado actuó "aprovechado el espacio angosto y extraño" para la víctima, "que él tapaba la única salida y ella se encontraba en estado de shock". La sentencia del Supremo subrayó que existió una primera agresión "sorpresiva, que ya por sí evidencia falta de consentimiento", a la que siguió una segunda efectuada expresamente "a pesar de la ausencia de consentimiento de la víctima". Los magistrados rechazaron la existencia de cualquier tipo de error sobre la voluntad de la mujer y que el hecho de que el deportista detuviera su acción cuando la joven se lo exigió "acredita el momento en que finalizó la actuación y explica que el Tribunal descartara la utilización de violencia o intimidación; no establece que la víctima hubiera consentido previamente ni que el acusado creyera que lo hacía". La resolución ha precisado que la mujer "presenta sintomatología ansiosa y depresiva grave relacionada con los hechos, habiendo resultado muy afectada su vida cotidiana, sufriendo trastorno de estrés postraumático crónico". El Supremo también desestimó el recurso interpuesto por la representación de la víctima, que solicitaba condenar al jugador a ocho años de cárcel por un delito de agresión sexual. Los magistrados rechazaron dicha pretensión al constatar que el relato de la primera instancia no describía que Mina hubiera utilizado "violencia con función instrumental" para doblegar la voluntad de la joven.

articles.title: La Comunidad de Madrid prosigue con la retirada de la concesión del estadio de Vallecas al Rayo
articles.standfirst: La Comisión Jurídica Asesora ha aprobado por unanimidad un dictamen que lo considera procedente
articles.summary: La Comisión Jurídica Asesora ha aprobado por unanimidad un dictamen que lo considera procedente
articles.body: Se le agota el tiempo al Rayo Vallecano. La Comisión Jurídica Asesora de la Comunidad de Madrid ha aprobado por unanimidad un dictamen que considera procedente la extinción de la concesión del campo de fútbol de Vallecas al cuadro franjirrojo. El marco legal establece que el procedimiento de extinción tiene un máximo de tramitación de ocho meses a partir de la fecha de incoación del expediente que es el 27 de julio. Por lo que durante el próximo mes de marzo de 2027 finalizará el plazo para resolver el procedimiento de extinción. El órgano consultivo, afirma que el procedimiento de la extinción de la concesión se debe al "incumplimiento de las obligaciones concesionales expuestas". “Han quedado acreditados de modo suficiente incumplimientos relevantes por parte del concesionario de las obligaciones que, conforme al título concesional, le correspondían, de modo que cabe apreciar procedente la extinción de la concesión pretendida por la Administración autonómica”, sostiene el dictamen. El escrito establece que el Rayo “ha incurrido en muy diversos incumplimientos de las obligaciones que le correspondían conforme a las cláusulas rectoras de la concesión”, referidos fundamentalmente a mantenimiento, conservación, inspecciones preceptivas y condiciones de seguridad, por lo que la extinción “resulta una medida proporcionada”. También constata que, “una vez incoado el expediente de extinción, se ha producido una mejora en el estado del bien objeto de la concesión y en la ejecución de esta”, si bien “esta mejora o subsanación de deficiencias, que afecta únicamente a parte de los incumplimientos, viene a confirmar la realidad de los mismos al tiempo de su incoación”. La retirada de la concesión sigue hacia delante y al Rayo se le agota el tiempo.

articles.title: USMNT's Mauricio Pochettino, Manchester United Reportedly Have 'Mutual' Interest amid Carrick Rumors
articles.summary: While Michael Carrick technically remains the manager at Manchester United, the club may have already identified his successor.
articles.body:
While Michael Carrick technically remains the manager at Manchester United, the club may have already identified his successor.

Pablo Iglesias Maurer and Jamie Jackson of the Guardian reported Tuesday there's mutual interest between the Red Devils and United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Pochettino signed a new contract with U.S. Soccer this August, with the idea to keep him in the role through the 2030 World Cup. The Athletic's Paul Tenorio, Tom Bogert and Henry Bushnell reported the buyout "is in the ballpark of $10 million."

Jason Burt of the Telegraph reported that Pochettino "is in no rush to leave the U.S. team." However, he's hopeful of returning to club management at some point and has been intrigued in the past by the challenge of coaching Manchester United.

Having Pochettino leave three months after giving him an extension would be less than ideal for U.S. Soccer. Ripping the bandage off now might be better than the alternative, though.

Even if he stays, this is something that could hang over the national team over the next few years. If he decides to accept a club position at a later point, that's less time for a new coach to execute their plan for the World Cup.

Manchester United hiring Pochettino would carry risk for both sides.

The 54-year-old took Southampton to an eighth-place finish in the Premier League in 2013-14 before moving on to Tottenham Hotspur. Spurs were PL runners-up in 2016-17 and third in 2015-16 and 2017-18. They also reached the Champions League final in 2018-19, losing to Liverpool.

While at Tottenham, Pochettino excelled at player development and delivered an entertaining style on the pitch.

Pochettino's subsequent spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea were far less memorable. His time with the U.S. national team is following along the same lines. A lot of the excitement surrounding the United States' performance in the group stage dissipated after a 4-1 hammering by Belgium in the round of 16.

Much like when it appointed José Mourinho in 2016, Manchester United might be getting Pochettino at a point when he's no longer a world-class manager.

From the coach's perspective, he'd be exchanging the relative stability of his current job for one of the most fraught in the sport.

For more than a decade after Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement, United has been mired in a cycle of dysfunction. It was too much to overcome for experienced managers such as Mourinho, Louis van Gaal and David Moyes along with Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, who built their profiles outside of England.

Given how far removed he is from his Tottenham peak, an underwhelming tenure at Manchester United could make it difficult for Pochettino to parachute into another major club.

In the event United officials look in another direction, ESPN's Rob Dawson reported in October that Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann could be serious candidates.

articles.title: Sky backs Equal Sport Project's pledges to improve equality through five shared ambitions across industry
articles.summary: Sky Sports is proud to support the Equal Sport Project, which is aiming to accelerate progress towards equality across sport through five shared ambitions; the project launches at a time when women’s sport is experiencing unprecedented momentum, yet significant inequalities remain
articles.body:
The Equal Sport Project unites sport in the UK behind five shared ambitions for women and men across sport - from local leisure centres to the biggest stadiums, and from grassroots pitches to boardrooms.

Major sporting organisations from across the UK's sporting landscape - including the FA, RFU, Youth Sport Trust, England Netball, UK Sport, LTA, Women's Sport Trust, Women in Sport, Team GB and Sport England - have made specific pledges to drive progress and help turn these ambitions into reality. Brands and broadcasters are also playing their part, signalling growing support for the movement across the wider sporting industry.

The rest of the industry is also being asked to commit support and pledges as the project seeks to gain momentum in the months and years to come.

The project launch comes at a time when the momentum of women's sport has never been stronger; participation is growing, audiences are growing and investment is accelerating.

But it also recognises that progress remains deeply uneven and that significant inequalities remain across all areas of the sporting system - from community and school sport right up to the highest levels.

Research published earlier this year by Sporting Insights found that fewer than 1 per cent of women working in sport believe gender equality has been achieved across the industry, while more than half believe they are paid less than men for carrying out the same role.

Women's sport also continues to receive a disproportionately small share of media coverage, accounting for around 9 per cent of broadcast sports coverage on key channels and 8 per cent of prime-time sports coverage. Meanwhile, gendered attitudes are increasing, with 41 per cent of boys agreeing some sports are for boys and nearly two-thirds (64 per cent) of girls want to be more active; confidence, body image, unequal facilities and gender stereotypes continue to present barriers to participation.

Accepting that there are already myriad priorities across the sector, The Equal Sport Project has identified five specific areas where collective leadership, investment and action will have the greatest impact and calls on the entire system to align behind them.

Equal access to sport for girls in school

Equal relevance, reach and revenue for women's sport

Governance structures redesigned for equality

This project is a call to action, which Sky is proud to support.

"For more than 30 years, Sky has backed women's sport," Sky Sports CEO Johnathan Licht wrote on LinkedIn .

"Today, we're the UK's leading investor in women's sports rights, investing in its growth and giving female athletes a platform on the biggest stage. "But visibility is only part of the story. Lasting change means breaking down the barriers that prevent girls from having the same opportunities to play, participate and stay in sport. "Our Game Changing research found that girls in the UK miss out on 280m hours of sport every year. That's a gap we're determined to help close. "That's why I'm proud that Sky is pledging its support to the Equal Sport Project. We'll continue to use our investment, platforms, partnerships and insight to grow women's sport, while going beyond broadcasting to create more opportunities for girls to participate. "Through initiatives including the Alessia Cup and our wider Game Changing work, we're focused on turning visibility into participation and helping create lasting change for women and girls in sport. "There's much more to do, and more to come from us on this soon. Collaboration across the industry will be critical if we're going to break down these barriers and close the gap."

articles.title: El Tenerife vuelve al trabajo con Jesús de Miguel siempre presente
articles.standfirst: La plantilla retoma los entrenamientos tras la semana más dolorosa de su historia reciente, arropada por Rayco García y el apoyo psicológico a disposición del vestuario
articles.summary: La plantilla retoma los entrenamientos tras la semana más dolorosa de su historia reciente, arropada por Rayco García y el apoyo psicológico a disposición del vestuario
articles.body: El Tenerife ha vuelto a pisar otra vez el césped. Lo ha hecho en la Ciudad Deportiva Javier Pérez, con la mirada puesta en el regreso a la competición, pero con el recuerdo de Jesús de Miguel todavía muy presente en cada rincón del vestuario. Una semana después de la tragedia que conmocionó al club y al fútbol español, la plantilla de Álvaro Cervera retomado la actividad en unos días que exigen mucho más que el simple esfuerzo físico. El trabajo ha recuperado su espacio en la rutina blanquiazul, aunque la ausencia de uno de los compañeros que hasta hace apenas unos días compartía entrenamientos, conversaciones y momentos cotidianos continúa siendo una realidad difícil de asimilar. El silencio que acompañó al equipo durante estos últimos días no desaparece con el regreso al campo. Tampoco lo hace el dolor. La vuelta representa, sencillamente, un paso necesario para seguir adelante sin dejar atrás a quien ya forma parte de la memoria colectiva del Tenerife. El máximo accionista de la entidad, Rayco García, acompañó al grupo en su regreso a la actividad deportiva después de una semana marcada por la pérdida, el funeral en Navahermosa y el homenaje celebrado el sábado en el Heliodoro Rodríguez López. El club también ha puesto a disposición de futbolistas, cuerpo técnico y personal de la entidad un equipo de psicólogos deportivos para ofrecer acompañamiento, tanto colectivo como individual, durante este proceso. La mirada comienza a dirigirse ahora a este domingo 15, fecha en la que el Tenerife recibirá al Ceuta en el Heliodoro. Álvaro Cervera y su cuerpo técnico tienen previsto completar una sesión diaria hasta el sábado, con el objetivo de recuperar progresivamente las dinámicas de trabajo y preparar el encuentro. La semana servirá también para que el equipo vuelva a familiarizarse con el balón después de todas las jornadas sin actividad sobre el césped. En ese recorrido, el regreso al Heliodoro durante algún entrenamiento podría adquirir un significado especial. Volver al escenario en el que se produjo la tragedia, lejos de la exigencia de un partido oficial, permitiría al grupo afrontar de manera progresiva un espacio inevitablemente asociado a los últimos acontecimientos. En el plano deportivo, Cervera deberá resolver algunas cuestiones de cara al encuentro ante el conjunto ceutí. La expulsión de Dani Martín frente al Andorra le impedirá participar por sanción, circunstancia que abre la puerta a Gabri de Vuyst para ocupar la portería. También habrá que seguir la evolución de César Álvarez, que arrastraba molestias en un dedo del pie, y comprobar si Gerard Valentín e Iván Chapela pueden incorporarse definitivamente a la dinámica del grupo después de sus respectivas lesiones musculares. La semana traerá, además, ausencias internacionales. Dani Fernández ha sido convocado por la selección española sub-19 para disputar la Ronda 2 de clasificación para el Europeo de Gales, mientras que Grant-Leon Ranos ha acudido a la llamada de Armenia para sus compromisos de la Nations League. El Tenerife vuelve a entrenar. Lo hace porque el calendario continúa y porque la vida del club necesita recuperar, poco a poco, sus espacios habituales. Pero en cada ejercicio, en cada conversación y en cada regreso al vestuario habrá un recuerdo que acompañará al grupo. Jesús de Miguel ya no estará para compartir el trabajo diario. Su lugar, sin embargo, permanece.

articles.title: Brennan Johnson: Wales forward says 'definitely more to come' after 50 caps
articles.summary: Brennan Johnson says he is happy with what he has achieved in football but would like to reach more major tournaments with Wales.
articles.body:
As he prepares to reach a personal milestone, Brennan Johnson says he is happy with what he has achieved in football - but would like to reach more major tournaments with Wales.

The 25-year-old Everton forward is set to make his 50th appearance against Norway in the Nations League on Saturday, becoming the third-youngest Welshman to reach the landmark after Ethan Ampadu and Chris Gunter.

Johnson has one major tournament under his belt - the 2022 World Cup - having missed out on selection for Euro 2020.

Wales failed to make this summer's World Cup, but have huge incentive to qualify for Euro 2028 with Cardiff named as one of eight host cities.

"Even when I think about having a Euros here now, it is special," said Johnson.

"We've got a good squad and a lot of players playing at a good level. Everyone knows it's coming up and it motivates us to work hard and show what we can do."

Wilson eyeing survival step as Wales tackle Norway

Wales call up MK Dons' Collins as Moore withdraws

Nottingham-born Johnson played for England at age-grade level before switching allegiances in 2018, a decision he has never regretted.

"As soon as I came to Wales I got a [good] feeling straight away and never looked back.

"You appreciate every cap for what it is, [50] kind of sneaks up on you a little bit.

"Playing at a World Cup was the highlight. It didn't go how we wanted it to, but I dreamed of playing at a World Cup from a young age.

"Qualifying for the World Cup the way we did in the play-offs was really special. Also my debut and scoring my first goal, big moments to look back on."

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live Sports Extra, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Johnson is hopeful there are more big moments to come, and believes Craig Bellamy's current Wales squad can draw inspiration from previous successes.

"There's a real confidence and I think it comes from the groups that were before," said Johnson recalling the side that reached the semi-finals of Euro 2016.

"Even before I was playing for Wales, the lads got far in the Euros and it gives you the confidence that it is possible.

"We want to carry on and raise the levels as much as we can. It's difficult because there were some unbelievable players in the past and it's hard to replicate directly against those players.

"But as a team we want to give everything we've got, that's a good place to be."

Johnson began his domestic career with Nottingham Forest, with his goals firing them into the Premier League in 2022 and keeping them in the top flight the following year.

His subsequent £47.5m move to Tottenham made him the second-most expensive Welsh signing after Gareth Bale, and it was his Europa League final winner against Manchester United that ended the club's 17-year trophy drought.

He joined Everton in the summer following a brief spell with Crystal Palace, and has only once found the net this season in the Carabao Cup.

But Johnson thinks the best is yet to come.

"There's definitely more to come and I'm excited for the next years," said Johnson.

"I'm really happy with what I've achieved in football. But at the same time I want to achieve more, especially with Wales.

articles.title: Greg Schiano will return as Rutgers coach in 2027, a decision that AD says serves program's 'best long-term interests'
articles.summary: Next season will mark Schiano's 19th total leading the Scarlet Knights, including his eighth consecutive in his second stint at the helm.
articles.body:
Rutgers is 2-7, and a meager 1-5 in Big Ten play, this season. The Scarlet Knights are already guaranteed to finish with a losing record for the second year in a row.

They're again in the basement of an 18-team conference that's seen Indiana and UCLA pull off instant turnarounds in recent years, and, yet, they're not making a change at the head-coaching position, Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn announced Tuesday .

The Scarlet Knights will be coached by Greg Schiano in 2027, Zinn said in a statement. While announcing his retention, she stressed her "obligation to make decisions that serve the best long-term interests" of Rutgers.

Next season will mark Schiano's 19th total leading the Scarlet Knights, including his eighth consecutive in his second stint at the helm.

"Let me be very clear: This decision is not reflective of a lowering of standards or an indication that everything is fine. It is not," Zinn said. "This is instead a reflection of my belief that we have an opportunity to make meaningful changes that will strengthen our roster and better position our program to compete and win at a higher level."

"Let me be very clear: This decision is not reflective of a lowering of standards or an indication that everything is fine. It is not," Zinn said.

"This is instead a reflection of my belief that we have an opportunity to make meaningful changes that will strengthen our roster and better position our program to compete and win at a higher level."

Zinn wrote that she and Schiano, 60, have met on several occasions to forecast what's ahead for the program, and she noted that she's encouraged by the plan he's concocted. As reported by ESPN , the hope is that having a defensive staff in place (Rutgers didn't hire a DC until February last cycle) and an uptick in transfer portal hits can help the program evolve.

"While we both recognize that plans alone do not produce wins, we share in a belief that necessary changes will help deliver the competitive results we all expect for our football program," she said.

Schiano first held the head-coaching title at Rutgers from 2001-2011. It took him a while, but he ultimately built the program into a Big East power. That sentence, though, suggests just how long ago that was, considering Big East football folded after the 2012 season .

His 2006 Rutgers team won 11 games — tied for the most in single-season program history — and ranked as high as No. 7 in the AP Top 25. With Ray Rice starring at running back and the Scarlet Knights trotting out a stifling defense that had twins Devin and Jason McCourty, Schiano's crew was formidable that season.

It was the start of something great in Piscataway, New Jersey. From 2006-2011, Rutgers won eight-plus games five times in a six-season span. That success paved the way for Schiano to land the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' head job. He occupied that post for only two seasons, however, and eventually returned to the collegiate ranks, where he was an assistant at Ohio State before being named Rutgers' leading man once more.

He took over in advance of the 2020 campaign and hasn't brought the Scarlet Knights back to the same level he had them at down the stretch of his first go-around.

Back-to-back 7-6 seasons in 2023 and 2024 were somewhat promising. In the latter, the the Scarlet Knights won four Big Ten games, their most in a season since joining the conference in 2014.

But, despite stronger quarterback play than it's often had — thanks to 2026 seventh-round pick and current Washington Commanders QB Athan Kaliakmanis — Rutgers regressed to 5-7 last season.

The Scarlet Knights' defense lagged, clocking out in the bottom 20 nationally in points per game allowed (31.8). That unit has been even worse this season, ranking 125th in the country with 32.4 points per game given up.

"Our 2026 football season has fallen well below our expectations and has understandably led to frustration from our passionate fans and supporters," Zinn said. "As your Director of Athletics and as a competitor at heart, I feel those same emotions. Our results are not acceptable for the expectations we have for our football program and for the athletics program we are building."

Zinn emphasized in her statement that she has faith in what Schiano has in store for the program and, more generally, "in what is possible at Rutgers."

Schiano, 101-115 all-time guiding the Scarlet Knights, is the program's winningest coach. His contract takes him through the 2029 season, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel , who also reported Tuesday that it would have cost Rutgers close to $28 million to dismiss the entire staff, with the school owing Schiano alone $18.6 million if he had been fired this year.

articles.standfirst: El concejal de Hortaleza, David Pérez, ha participado en el acto junto a los alumnos del colegio que tiene el nombre del legendario jugador del Real Madrid
articles.summary: El concejal de Hortaleza, David Pérez, ha participado en el acto junto a los alumnos del colegio que tiene el nombre del legendario jugador del Real Madrid
articles.body: El concejal de Hortaleza, David Pérez, ha asistido al acto homenaje a Alfredo Di Stéfano que se ha celebrado en el Colegio de Educación Infantil, Primaria y Secundaria Obligatoria del distrito que lleva su nombre, con motivo del centenario del nacimiento del deportista. Con esta iniciativa, se ha acercado a los alumnos de primero de primaria la trayectoria vital y profesional de un referente universal del fútbol, además de ensalzar valores del deporte como “la convivencia, el respeto o la tolerancia”, que se personalizan también en Ricardo Gallego, embajador de la Fundación Real Madrid, presente en el acto. Integrante de la Quinta del Buitre e internacional con la selección española, el concejal de Hortaleza ha definido a Gallego como “uno de los mejores jugadores de la historia”, además de una persona “sencilla y de valores” que es “ejemplo” para todos los jóvenes. Durante el acto, los alumnos han recorrido el mural dedicado a Di Stéfano, han visto un vídeo sobre su trayectoria y han leído el manifiesto por el ‘Deporte Limpio’. Además, Ricardo Gallego, que conoció personalmente a Di Stéfano, ha ofrecido su testimonio a los escolares donde les ha transmitido que el éxito es fruto de la constancia, el respeto y la dedicación diaria. La jornada ha servido también para impulsar la colaboración entre instituciones educativas, deportivas y municipales, con la participación del colegio, la Fundación Real Madrid y la Junta Municipal de Hortaleza.

articles.title: Manchester United: Michael Carrick future to be discussed at Monaco meeting
articles.summary: Manchester United's power brokers meet in Monaco on Wednesday to decide whether Michael Carrick will remain as head coach
articles.body:
Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach will be determined 800 miles away from Old Trafford in Monaco on Wednesday.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are flying out for one of their regular pre-planned meetings to discuss strategy around the football club.

On this occasion, the main issue to be decided is Carrick's future and what should happen next.

It is expected that Berrada and Wilcox's recommendation is for the head coach to go.

It is not a situation Sir Jim Ratcliffe can have expected to find himself in again, less than three years after purchasing a minority stake in United.

On Christmas Eve 2023, his vision was much different.

"Our shared ambition is clear: we all want to see Manchester United back where we belong, at the very top of English, European and world football," he said.

Instead, United are 18th, in the Premier League's relegation zone after winning just one of their first 10 games and none since August. It is their lowest position so far into a top-flight season since 1986-87 when they were 20th.

Ratcliffe has been criticised for many decisions since he bought his 28.94% stake for just over £1bn. This is one he really needs to get right.

Why is the meeting taking place in Monaco?

Ratcliffe's home is in Monaco and his company Ineos has offices in the principality.

The meeting had been in the diary for some time as a regular catch-up between senior executives and their boss.

Sources have stressed that the choice of location was not influenced by the debate around Carrick's future - it just happens to now be the most important item for discussion.

The decision to sack United's previous two managers was not made in a meeting in Monaco.

Ruben Amorim was sacked 19 hours after his explosive media conference following a 1-1 draw at Leeds in January.

Erik ten Hag went a day after Manchester United lost at West Ham leaving them with just three wins from their opening nine matches

A decision to sack Dutchman Ten Hag was taken at a meeting of senior Ineos executives in the summer of 2024, only for the choice to be reversed following the FA Cup final triumph over Manchester City.

Four months later there was a six-hour meeting at Ineos HQ in London as Ten Hag's tenure hung by a thread. He survived again but was gone three weeks later.

Amorim was summoned to Monaco after the Europa League final defeat to Tottenham in 2025.

There is daily contact between senior executives so if the meeting was purely to decide Carrick's fate, it could be done by video conference and the need to travel to Monaco is not the reason why there is yet to be a decision.

The travel element does add a complication given the preference for Berrada and Wilcox is to inform Carrick of any decision face to face.

Sources say the Monaco meetings used to be held every six weeks, although in more recent times they are less frequent.

Those who have attended them say they take place in the morning, tend to last between three and four hours and usually stop on time so Ratcliffe can go for his regular lunchtime jog.

Pochettino, Howe, Emery... or Carrick? Man Utd's managerial options

What Howe could bring to Man Utd - and what are the challenges?

United stood by Carrick after the woeful 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October.

Club sources were adamant they wanted to give Carrick and his players a chance to turn the situation around it was also felt that the two-week international break in November represented a better chance for the club to properly assess the club's start to the campaign.

However, although they did end a long wait for a victory against Roma on 3 November, United had to come from two goals down to seal a 3-2 victory in a chaotic game.

They failed to press home their advantage after excelling in the first half against Chelsea and eventually lost 2-0 as experienced central defender Lisandro Martinez was sent off.

On Sunday, they conceded twice inside five minutes and had to come from two goals down twice to claim a point against Villa.

While sources said the comebacks showed the United squad were still playing for Carrick, it is also understood the chaotic nature of the games and the inability to stop the opposition from scoring has led Berrada and Wilcox, who were at all three matches, to conclude a change of coach is required to get United out of the mess they find themselves in.

United have conceded 30 goals so far this season in 15 games - 19 in 10 Premier League matches, eight in four in the Champions League and three in their one Carabao Cup tie.

Instead of replacing Carrick another option under consideration is additional coaching support to assist the current team.

Bayern Munich coach Aaron Danks, who worked with Carrick at Middlesbrough and was touted as a potential appointment in the summer, is one option.

If Ratcliffe was to decide otherwise, it would raise serious questions over the future of Berrada and Wilcox.

How could they work with Carrick again in that scenario?

The pair have been the subject of intense and frequent fan discontent. But sources are adamant that Ratcliffe still retains faith in the pair, even though United are heading towards sacking a manager in mid-season for the third successive year, having backed them in the summer and spend millions on new players.

Ratcliffe is a ruthless operator, and has clear opinions of his own. He also has form, spending £5m hiring Dan Ashworth as sporting director from Newcastle in 2024, then waiting for the 55-year-old to spend five months on gardening leave before he could start work.

Five months later, Ashworth was sacked due to a divergence of opinion over who should replace Ten Hag. Ashworth felt someone with Premier League experience was a better fit for United's squad. Ratcliffe wanted a more modern alternative. Berrada suggested Amorim. Wilcox, after initial reservations, also got on board. Amorim was dismissed after 14 months.

The other unknown element is the Glazer family. They will need to sign off any decision.

At the time of the Ratcliffe purchase, United confirmed the club's 'board' had handed over responsibility for the football side. But United's articles of association state that responsibilities delegated by directors can also be "revoked or altered".

Crucially, of the 12 current directors, six are members of the Glazer family, including co-chairs Joel and Avi Glazer. United's rules state that if required, the chairman of any meeting will have a second and casting vote.

Although there have been media reports of Glazer dissatisfaction at United's current plight, there has been no public statement on the matter.

What is Carrick scheduled to be doing for the next couple of days?

It may seem strange, but the reality is, as with any employee, Carrick will continue to do his job until told otherwise - and so far, there has been no conversation to that effect.

Although most of his squad, and a significant number of academy players, are on international duty, a core remains at home.

This includes Mason Mount, Joshua Zirkzee and Matthijs de Ligt. Harry Maguire, who suffered a back spasm against Villa, is also there, as are other injured players, including Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford.

Carrick gave his players a day off on Monday but scheduled training days for Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. After that, they are not due to report back until 17 November, by which time the international contingent should start to return and begin preparations for the trip to Liverpool on 22 November.

"Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so, but as a normal international week is, we'll have some training and we'll have one or two days off," Carrick said after the Villa game. "Not too much. But we'll train and get ready for the next game."

Who might be discussed as a possible replacement for Carrick?

If the discussions go as anticipated, replacing Carrick will be a key element.

Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a leading contender and is known to be keen on the job.

United spoke to the former Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea boss about their managerial position on three different occasions - first of all when Jose Mourinho was sacked in 2018, then in 2022 when the club decided on Ten Hag instead and then again when the Dutchman was sacked.

The obvious problem is that Pochettino currently has a job as head coach of the United States. He renewed his contract in August and has a two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti over the next week. The Argentine, 54, is due to speak to the media on Friday and has a $10m (£7.5m) release clause.

Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe is out of work and available. BBC Sport has reported the compensation due to his old club if Manchester United appointed thr 48-year-old now would be £3m. But it reduces as the season goes on and would be nothing in the summer.

Italian Antonio Conte is also thought to be keen and the 57-year-old has Premier League title-winning experience at Chelsea and more recently won Serie A with Napoli last season, before leaving the club.

Julian Nagelsmann stood down as Germany boss in the wake of their last-32 exit at the World Cup exit at the World Cup but the German, 39, won the Bundesliga title with Bayern Munich in 2022-23.

Kieran McKenna was part of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's coaching team at Manchester United and left Ipswich after four-and-a-half years this summer. However, it is felt more likely United would want a candidate with greater experience than the 40-year-old Northern Irishman.

Where does this all leave Carrick? In a unenviable position of carrying on as if it was business as usual when the reality is anything but.

articles.title: El Lugo sigue derribando 'murallas'
articles.standfirst: Iguala el gran arranque del Castellón 2023-2024 que subió a Segunda
articles.summary: Iguala el gran arranque del Castellón 2023-2024 que subió a Segunda
articles.body: No hay nadie más fuerte en Primera Federación que el Club Deportivo Lugo. El equipo de la ciudad amurallada es una roca en este arranque de temporada. 28 puntos de 33 posibles, ganando 9 de sus 11 encuentros. O sea, todos, menos el de Ponferrada (0-0) y el de Irún, donde cosechó su única (y dolorosa) derrota, contra el Real Unión (4-1). De esta manera, los albivermellos han igualado el gran inicio de curso del Castellón en la temporada 2023-2024, en la que los orelluts lograron el ansiado regreso a la categoría de plata como campeones del Grupo II. Aquel equipo sumó 46 puntos en la primera vuelta y terminó la Liga con 82. La renta que atesoran los lucenses con sus perseguidores es brutal. Ya son 10 puntos de ventaja sobre el 3º (Pontevedra), 11 sobre el Racing Ferrol y el Mirandés (su próximo rival). Le saca 13 a la Ponferradina y 15 a la Cultural. Todos ellos llamados, a priori, a pelear por el ascenso. El único que parece seguirle el rastro no muy de lejos es la UD Logroñés, que es 2º en la clasificación, a 5 puntos de los gallegos, y que cayó derrotada en el Anxo Carro. El Club Divertido Lugo es, además, el único club de los 40 que componen la Primera Federación que lo ganado todo en su estadio (5/5). El líder del otro grupo, el Real Zaragoza, cedió un empate en el Ibercaja Estadio y su margen al frente de la tabla es mucho más reducido. Esta es su cuarta temporada seguida en la categoría de bronce (bajó en 2023 tras 11 años ininterrumpidos en Segunda). En su primera campaña, terminó la primera vuelta con 26 puntos. En la segunda, con 23. Y en la tercera, la pasada y mejor de todas, con 29. Ahora suma 28 cuando todavía quedan ocho jornadas para que el campeonato llegue a su ecuador. Las cosas han cambiado desde la llegada al banquillo de Borja Fernández, que viene de lograr sus ascensos consecutivos con la UD Ourense, el equipo de su ciudad. Pero son conscientes de que queda mucho. Porque, como dicen allí, en Lugo hai que sachar ata o final.

articles.title: Liga de dos
articles.standfirst: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.summary: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.body: Perdón por interrumpir, pero resulta que, disputadas 12 jornadas de campeonato doméstico, va para un tercio ya, ni Barcelona ni Real Madrid han perdido un solo punto contra un equipo situado por debajo del cuarto puesto. ¡Ni uno! Los que echa de menos el Barça se los quedó directamente el Madrid, los que echa de menos el Madrid se los embolsaron Betis y Atlético. Lo demás, todo victorias. Holgadas unas cuantas, menos lucidas otras, victorias al fin y al cabo. Hay que conceder así a los equipos de Simeone y Pellegini el mérito de que con siete meses de competición aún por delante ésta no sea ya del todo Liga de dos, pero conviene matizar que el notable arranque rojiblanco no da para liderato (ni para segundo puesto ya) o que el notable arranque verdiblanco no da para podio. Los demás se van quedando por el camino, apenas Real Sociedad y Sevilla sin que como mínimo los doble en puntuación el primer clasificado. No falta quien, en cuanto se hacen este tipo de consideraciones, corra raudo a poner el ejemplo de otras Ligas europeas en las que uno gana siempre (el que se manejaba la semana pasada en La Cerámica) y otro gana casi siempre (el que se manejaba la semana pasada en el Metropolitano), pero eso es porque mal de muchos equivale a consuelo de tontos y porque en realidad a casi todo el personal ya le va bien con este duopolio frente al que sólo ha parecido rebelarse en los últimos años don Diego Pablo. Que así recibe el trato que recibe, ésa es otra. Partiendo de los derechos televisivos y abarcando todo lo que se nos pueda ocurrir, la Liga se organiza para que sea efectivamente de dos, lo que por otra parte tiene sendas consecuencias lamentables: que cuando uno de ellos amenaza con descogarse haya que hacer lo posible y lo imposible para mantenerlo (por lo civil o por lo criminal, que diría Luis) y que el resto, al tiempo, termine tirando directamente de suplentes cuando el calendario dicte visita al dentista, poco dispuestos los entrenadores a perder efectivos además de perder puntos. Liga de dos, en fin. Que por momentos es de tres y que vaya usted a saber si podría ser de cuatro, pero Liga de dos en lo que al deseo general de los barandas respecta. Luego que si todo está polarizado...

articles.summary: El centrocampista del Real Madrid no pudo completar el entrenamiento de Francia de este martes y se someterá a pruebas
articles.body: Alarma Tchouaméni en Francia. El centrocampista del Madrid no pudo completar el entrenamiento de la selección francesa de este martes y se someterá a pruebas para determinar el alcance de sus molestias en la ingle. Según informa L'Équipe, podría abandonar la concentración de Les Bleus y perderse los próximos compromisos internacionales. La preocupación se centra ahora en conocer la naturaleza exacta de la lesión. Francia viajará a Italia este jueves y recibirá a Turquía el domingo en sus dos próximos encuentros de la Liga de Naciones. Tras las bajas de Pierre Kalulu y Marcus Thuram, Zidane podría tener que prescindir también del futbolista del Madrid, que ya se perdió la anterior convocatoria de septiembre-octubre. Entonces, Zidane decidió dejarlo en Madrid al considerar que todavía no estaba en condiciones físicas óptimas, después de la lesión en el aductor que sufrió durante el Mundial de Estados Unidos. El Real Madrid apunta que Tchouaméni sufre molestias en la zona inguinal derecha. El centrocampista ha tenido que retirarse del entrenamiento y, según trasladan desde el club blanco, a poco que persistan esas molestias regresará este miércoles a Madrid. En Valdebebas siguen pendientes de recibir la comunicación oficial de la Federación Francesa... y de un regreso que obligará a Mourinho a planificar los siguientes pasos con el francés.

articles.title: Fifa presidency: University lecturer bidding to challenge Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: University lecturer Peter Auf der Heyde is seeking to be nominated to take on Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency.
articles.body:
University lecturer Peter Auf der Heyde is launching an ambitious attempt to take on Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency.

The former journalist and football club owner is seeking to be nominated to challenge the incumbent Infantino - and wants to be paid a salary of just $1 (75p) per year if he wins the role.

South African Auf der Heyde lectures in journalism at Southampton Solent University and was previously sports editor of the Deutsche Presse-Agentur (dpa) in Germany.

He was president of the Grahamstown Soccer Association in South Africa and both owned and managed second-division side UDW FC in the early 1990s.

"I feel very strongly that there needs to be a challenge in any election," Auf der Heyde told BBC Radio Solent.

"There should not be an uncontested election and in this case Infantino needs to be challenged. It's important for accountability and transparency."

For Auf der Heyde to become a candidate to challenge Infantino in the March 2027 election, he will need to be nominated by five football associations.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is also considering standing against the current president, who faced calls to stand down following a controversial plan to sell off stakes in the governing body's competitions to private investors.

Infantino insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football, and laughed off questions about whether he had considered resigning his position.

He is seeking a fourth and final term in the role but is also facing competition from Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association, and former Tottenham Hotspur and Switzerland defender Ramon Vega.

The deadline for candidates to confirm they are standing against Infantino is 18 November.

"I'm not asking for countries to vote for me, I'm asking for them to nominate me," added Auf der Heyde.

"Once you have a nomination and become an official candidate you can then ask questions [to other candidates] that you can't ask otherwise.

"Infantino earned around $6m (£4.49m) last year which I think is ridiculous. I would suggest that $450,000 (£337,259) is a very adequate salary and in my case I would ask to be paid $1 per year and after four years if I have maintained my promises then I can get the remaining money."

Wenger considers standing against Infantino

'Emerging nations World Cup' part of manifesto

Auf der Heyde revealed that so far he has written to all 211 of Fifa's member associations, with replies already from the Jamaican and English Football Associations.

He broke down his manifesto for the role into three sections, with a key part of that being a new global competition for smaller footballing nations.

Only 48 nations qualify for the men's World Cup finals every four years with 163 missing out.

"I'd like to see an emerging nations World Cup," said Auf der Heyde, who covered 13 consecutive Africa Cup of Nations as a journalist.

"This would be for countries like Eswatini, Andorra and San Marino, who will quite frankly never qualify for the World Cup.

"They should be allowed in my view to play for a global competition where only these kind of countries have a chance to play.

"It would be wonderful if winning teams from that competition could then qualify further for the World Cup."

articles.title: Partick Thistle lose SWPL points for amateur player payments
articles.summary: Partick Thistle are deducted three points and fined £6,000 by the Scottish Women's Premier League for making payments to players who were registered as amateurs last season.
articles.body:
Partick Thistle have been deducted three points and fined £6,000 by the Scottish Women's Premier League for making payments to players who were registered as amateurs last season.

Thistle finished sixth last season and the points penalty means they slip one place to second bottom spot, three points behind Spartans, in the current 10-team table.

It follows a hearing on Monday at which the Glasgow club were found to be in breach of rules about making payments to amateur registered players and "submitting incorrect information regarding the submission of the certificate and undertaking document required as part of the membership criteria process".

Half of Thistle's fine is suspended until the end of season.

Thistle had the right of appeal but said on their website that the club "acknowledges and accepts the verdict".

They add: "The circumstances which led to the breach of SWPL player rule 37 and competition rule E31.11 were a result of a failure of internal process, which has since been addressed and resolved so that it can not occur in future.

"The club admitted the breach immediately when brought to our attention.

"We apologise to our fans for the mistake and its consequences."

Bottom side Aberdeen are now only four points behind Thistle.

articles.title: El 'presi' del Oviedo, sobre Raúl: "El Madrid nos dijo: 'ni lo penséis, es vuestro entrenador'"
articles.standfirst: MARCA entrevista a Martín Peláez, presidente del Oviedo, en Pachuca (México)
articles.summary: MARCA entrevista a Martín Peláez, presidente del Oviedo, en Pachuca (México)
articles.body: Martín Peláez, presidente del Real Oviedo, atiende a MARCA en el marco del Salón de la Fama del Fútbol de Pachuca, México, ciudad que da nombre al Grupo Pachuca, propietaria del Real Oviedo. Peláez sabe que el fichaje de Raúl ha tenido en España una dimensión nacional. Pregunta. Raúl es el hombre de la semana en España y su nuevo entrenador. ¿Qué me dice? Respuesta. En Oviedo lo afrontamos con mucha ilusión, aunque estamos muy agradecidos por todo el trabajo que ha hecho el cuerpo técnico anterior [Julián Calero] para construir este Oviedo. Como decía, estamos muy ilusionados, como cuando llega cualquier persona, entrenador o jugador. Pero evidentemente Raúl es un personaje que solo con su nombre ya se presenta por sí solo. La verdad es que estamos muy contentos. P. ¿Por qué Raúl González Blanco? ¿Qué les llevó a apostar por él? R. Nosotros buscamos un entrenador que nos pueda dar lo que queremos. Se sabe cuál es nuestra filosofía de gestión. Partiendo de un grupo, queremos un equipo valiente, que sienta, que trate de jugar bien al fútbol y que vaya a buscar los partidos. Quizá son demasiadas cosas que pedir, pero pensamos que Raúl tiene ese perfil. Después veremos si sale bien o no, pero creemos que reúne esas características. Además, David Hernández, nuestro director deportivo, conoce muy bien su trabajo en el Castilla. La apuesta es por él. P. ¿La elección responde también a la personalidad que es Raúl, a lo que representa, más allá de su trayectoria como futbolista? R. Por supuesto. No es solamente el jugador que ha sido, sino también la personalidad que es. Eso va a generar un sentimiento positivo, sin duda. P. Muchos oviedistas se preguntan si el cambio responde a una cuestión de resultados, de puntos, porque el equipo todavía está en la pelea, o si tiene más que ver con el estilo de juego. R. Sí, por supuesto. No estamos tan mal posicionados en la clasificación ni tan lejos del 'playoffs', pero la verdad es que no estábamos viendo al Oviedo que queríamos ver. Queremos un Oviedo diferente. Aquí no buscamos culpables; los principales responsables somos nosotros, porque somos quienes tomamos las decisiones sobre los entrenadores. Pero sí queremos ver un equipo distinto. P. ¿Han hablado con gente del Real Madrid, incluso con Florentino Pérez, sobre este fichaje? ¿Alguien les recomendó a Raúl? Siempre se ha dicho que Raúl ha sido uno de los mejores técnicos que ha pasado por la cartera del club blanco en los últimos años. R. Sí, la verdad es que hemos hablado con gente del entorno del Madrid. De todas las personas con las que hablamos, me quedo con varias opiniones, pero hubo una persona que me dijo: 'No lo penséis, no os lo penséis. Raúl es el entrenador que buscáis, vuestro entrenador'. P. Y la última, ¿están preparados para la avalancha mediática que se avecina en Oviedo? Usted es mexicano, pero conoce perfectamente la dimensión que tiene el nombre de Raúl González Blanco en España y todo lo que representa mediáticamente. R. Claro. De hecho, ya lo sabíamos, aunque quizá no habíamos dimensionado lo que suponía. Esta mañana se lo comentaba a mis compañeros de Oviedo que nos acompañan en esta ceremonia del Salón de la Fama. Todos los días, Laura, nuestra jefa de comunicación, me pasa el dossier de prensa con todo lo que se habla del Oviedo. Normalmente son entre 15 y 25 páginas. Hoy el informe llegó a 139. ¡El primer día de Raúl! Ahí te das cuenta de la importancia que tiene. Ya lo sabíamos, pero hasta que no lo ves, no terminas de dimensionarlo.

Martín, con el redactor de MARCA.

articles.title: El Real Madrid abre la lata
articles.standfirst: Caruso, Beerensteyn y Caicedo desatascan el partido en la segunda parte y firman la primera victoria blanca en la fase Liga
articles.summary: Caruso, Beerensteyn y Caicedo desatascan el partido en la segunda parte y firman la primera victoria blanca en la fase Liga
articles.body: El Real Madrid logró su primera victoria en la fase Liga de la Champions al imponerse (3-0) al Paris FC en un Alfredo Di Stéfano que apenas contó con 952 espectadores en las gradas. Quesada sorprendió dando entrada en el once a tres campeonas del mundo Sub'20 -véase Laia, Cristóbal e Irune-. El conjunto blanco comenzó frío, como el tiempo en la capital, y lento. Tanto es así que el técnico pidió más intensidad a las suyas, sobre todo en faceta defensiva. Las primeras ocasiones fueron tímidas. Un pase lateral de Eva que Schröder no llegó a conectar; un cabezazo de Andersson a la salida de un córner que se estrelló contra el muro defensivo galo; o un disparo desde la medialuna de Athenea que acabó en las manos de Seweryn. Luego Caruso estrelló un tímido cabezazo en el travesaño, lo único salvable de una primera parte aburrida. El paso por vestuarios dejó a Athenea fuera de juego y al equipo sin extremos naturales, por lo que no fue de extrañar que el gol con el que se abriese la lata llegara por dentro. Un robo de Jacinto y una buena conducción de Cristóbal dio pie al disparo de Schröder y parada de Seweryn, cuyo rechace aprovechó Caruso para mandar el balón a la jaula. La sueca, que no estuvo fina de cara a gol, ejerció de asistente en el segundo apenas diez minutos después. Lo hizo con un pase entre líneas para la llegada de Beerensteyn, que fusiló a la meta rival para aumentar la renta blanca. Schröder volvería aparecer en el tramo final para combinar con Caicedo, que apenas necesitó un toque sutil para anotar el tercero. El Real Madrid se mantiene invicto en una Champions en la que tiene el objetivo de romper la barrera de los cuartos de final. De momento, aún debe recibir al Inter de Milán y visitar el feudo de la Roma para completar esta fase y acceder a la ronda de eliminatorias.

articles.title: El Alavés no da opción al Anaitasuna
articles.standfirst: Los babazorros golearon al cuadro guipuzcoano con un doblete de Mariano
articles.summary: Los babazorros golearon al cuadro guipuzcoano con un doblete de Mariano
articles.body: la tercera fue la vencida. Después de que los aficionados del Anaitasuna vieran cómo se suspendía en dos ocasiones el esperado encuentro copero ante el Alavés, Txerloia acogió este martes la visita de un Primera. Los babazorros no dieron opción al conjunto guipuzcoano y golearon para lograr el primer triunfo del curso a domicilio. Le costó encarrilar el partido a un Alavés que no abrió la lata hasta la media hora de juego. Jonny, con un potente disparo desde fuera del área, hizo el primero de la tarde. Poco después, Mariano doblaría la ventaja en el marcador tras culminar una buena jugada por la derecha. Juaristi recortó diferentes para devolver la esperanza a Txerloia. Sin embargo, el Alavés pisó el acelerador tras la reanudación. Miguel Rodríguez se estrenó como goleador después de una gran asistencia de Aleñá y Mariano firmó el doblete tras una buena acción de Ángel Pérez. Mañas se sumó a la goleadora babazorra en una excelente jugada individual y Aleñá hizo el sexto. Los hombres de Quique cumplieron con el trámite y ahora disfrutaran del parón antes de encarar la recta final de 2026 en la que están obligados a levantar el vuelo después de ocho jornadas sin conocer el triunfo. Al menos, la victoria en Copa les permite recuperar sensaciones perdidas.

articles.title: Sorloth, en duda
articles.standfirst: La continuidad del 9 más allá de enero es otro tema a debate en el Atlético. Su salida abriría la puerta al fichaje de otro atacante
articles.summary: La continuidad del 9 más allá de enero es otro tema a debate en el Atlético. Su salida abriría la puerta al fichaje de otro atacante
articles.body: Más allá del objetivo prioritario de contratar a un 3 como recambio de Grimaldo, el Atlético aborda más frentes de cara al próximo mercado invernal. Entre ellos, el de un Sorloth que cada día genera más controversia y que, en el caso de salir en enero, abriría la puerta a la llegada de otro atacante. Queda tiempo, muchos partidos por delante y más argumentos para alimentar el debate, pero es uno más de los escenarios que se contemplan en el Metropolitano. De lo que no hay duda es que su estatus en el club ha cambiado radicalmente: lo que en verano era innegociable, es una vía a explorar en invierno. Dicho de otro modo, si hace unos meses su continuidad en la plantilla estaba asegurada, ahora pasa a ser objeto de estudio. Las circunstancias han cambiado y su rendimiento sobre el verde tampoco ayuda. Aún por estrenarse como goleador tras seis apariciones en este curso (cierto es que apenas ha disputado 155 minutos tras empezar lastrado por los dos meses que estuvo lesionado en el verano), los dos últimos compromisos le ponen en el foco. Frente al Bayern fue el arma de Simeone para saltar la presión alta, pero apenas ganó un duelo a los centrales. Contra el Barcelona, ante el que irrumpió como revulsivo sin llegar a cambiar nada, su lenguaje corporal aumentó las sospechas. Tanto que su posible salida ya se ve de otra manera. No hay que olvidar que en el verano, con el culebrón de Julián Alvarez en pleno apogeo, se trataba del único 9 seguro a disposición de Simeone. Pero además existía otra circunstancia que cerraba las puertas a su adiós, pues el Villarreal se había guardado un 20% de una futura venta en los dos siguientes años durante la operación sellada con el Atlético en agosto de 2024. Dos condicionantes a los que se une ahora que Jonathan David, aterrizado el último día del mercado, ha logrado pasar de 'incógnita' a alternativa de garantías para el ataque, especialmente tras marcar en sus tres primeras apariciones ligueras. Así las cosas, pese a que el noruego es el único con unas características diferentes al resto de delanteros del Atlético, su rol en el equipo sigue ofreciendo dudas. De ahí que ya no se vería con malos ojos un cambio de aires en invierno, implicando su hipotético adiós que Mateu Alemany se lanzara a la búsqueda de otro atacante con más impacto en el juego. Una posibilidad que incluso podría satisfacer al propio Sorloth, reacio a aceptar la suplencia a la que ha sido abocado prácticamente desde su llegada, si su cuota de minutos sigue a la baja. Incluso desde el punto de vista de la rentabilidad de su fichaje, el Atlético también estaría ante el momento idóneo para su traspaso, pues con contrato hasta 2028, sería esta ventana de enero o la del próximo verano las últimas en las que aún podría hacer caja. De ahí que, a la espera de propuestas, lo único seguro es que Sorloth encara el final de año en un escenario nuevo.

articles.title: Parrott in running for hat-trick at FAI awards
articles.summary: Troy Parrott is shortlisted in three categories for the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) International Awards.
articles.body:
Troy Parrott has been shortlisted in three categories for the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) International Awards.

The 24-year-old Real Betis striker is in the running for player of the year and young player of the year, while he has two nominations for goal of the year.

Parrott helped propel the Republic of Ireland into the World Cup playoffs, scoring both goals in the victory over Portugal in Dublin before netting a hat-trick in the must-win away game against Hungary, while also finding the net from the spot in the play-off defeat by Czech Republic.

The Dubliner is a first-time nominee in the player of the year category, joined by Dara O'Shea who also makes the list for the first time, while goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher makes the shortlist for the second year.

James Abankwah and Evan Ferguson - who won in 2022 and 2023 - join Parrott on the young player of the year shortlist.

Parrott's second goal and last-gasp winner away to Hungary are in consideration for goal of the year along with Katie McCabe's stunning stike in the 3-2 away win against Poland in a World Cup qualifier.

The women's national team captain is nominated for women's senior player of the year for a sixth time and the 2021 winner is joined by first-time nominees Emily Murphy and Marissa Sheva.

Women's young player of the year will be contested between 2024 winner Jessie Stapleton, three-time nominee Abbie Larkin and Emily Murphy who is included for the first time.

Jacob Devaney, Mason Melia and Jamie Mullins are nominated for the men's under-21 award.

The performances taken into account for all categories are from June 2025 to May 2026

articles.title: Morgan Park High School students walk out after football team staff changes
articles.summary: Students, parents and alumni walked out of Morgan Park High School Tuesday morning after the school's football coach is out after a winning season.
articles.body:
Hundreds of students, parents and alumni walked out of Morgan Park High School Tuesday morning after the school's football coach is out after a winning season.

As soon as word got out that the coach was out, parents started organizing, saying they want answers for their kids.

The Morgan Park Mustangs had a strong season, winning back-to-back city titles.

And despite losing in the state playoffs, players thought they had one more Friday night together during the Prep Bowl semifinal.

"It's really sad," freshman football player Owmar Robinson said. "We were sad when we lost our game and then we thought we were going to play like 3 more games with the seniors but now we can't even do that so that really broke my heart for real."

In an email to football families Monday, the principal said the team couldn't play Friday because of the change in leadership.

The principal said James had told families this would be his last season at Morgan Park and that he'd accepted another coaching job.

But in a post on Instagram, James said he never resigned or accepted another job.

He said he told the school he'd decide his future at the end of the season and that the school asked him to turn in his keys and relieved him of his duties.

"I'm a little bit upset because I was excited even if I was performing or not because I was going to go," sophomore poms performer Joselyn Jones said.

The school also canceled the rest of the team's practices.

The athletic director is expected to follow up with families about returning equipment.

Football mom Maritza Morales said it felt like the decision came out of left field.

"They're devastated," she said. "They're hurt. They're confused. They don't know what's going on. They are trying to figure out what they did wrong. And they didn't do anything wrong. They did exactly what they were supposed to do." Parents are also frustrated they can no longer access film from the games.

"It's about the boys," football mom Lauren Waithe said. "To take them out of the rest of their football season. You have seniors that are depending on scholarships to go to school. Horrible."

The controversy is garnering attention from alumni like state Representative Kam Buckner... who played with James at Morgan Park and in college.

In a post on social media he wrote... "our young men deserve answers."

Chicago Public Schools said principals make personnel decisions and the district doesn't comment on those matters.

"We just want answers," Morales said. "We want to figure out what's going on and why we can't participate in the Prep Bowl. Why did you decide to do that in the middle of the season when we still had a chance to win another title."

The coach just released a new statement Tuesday also urging the school to make sure the kids have access to their game films for recruiting purposes.

The school wants to name a new coach by Jan. 1 and says it will ask players and families for input.

Morgan Park lost in the playoffs to Providence Catholic. They too fired their coach mid-season, despite a winning record.

CPS said in a statement, "Chicago Public Schools understands the importance of the HUDL software and its crucial role in game planning, streaming, scouting and recruiting to support potential college scholarships. Morgan Park's HUDL subscription expired this week, causing a temporary loss of access for all users. Morgan Park administration, with support from the District, is working with the company this afternoon to renew its subscription and restore access to the platform as soon as possible."

articles.title: Sebastien Pocognoli: Scotland boss to lean on Scott McTominay in his 'captain group of five'
articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli is delighted to welcome "exciting" Scott McTominay into his squad, saying the Napoli midfielder is one of the "fantastic leaders" that helped persuade him to become Scotland head coach.
articles.body:
Sebastien Pocognoli is delighted to welcome "exciting" Scott McTominay into his squad, saying the Napoli midfielder is one of the "fantastic leaders" that helped persuade him to become Scotland head coach.

The Belgian revealed the fit-again 29-year-old "is in my captain group of five", who will be relied upon to make sure his instructions are carried out on the field of play.

McTominay missed Pocognoli's first, four-game Uefa Nations League camp in charge as Scotland drew with Slovenia, lost to Switzerland, beat North Macedonia, but then lost the return at home to the Slovenians.

The midfielder, who is back playing after a minor heart procedure, has revealed he received treatment to correct an irregular heartbeat two days before Scotland's World Cup win over Haiti in June.

"I don't have to paint a picture of how important a player he is for us," said Pocognoli as he prepared for Friday's meeting with North Macedonia at Hampden.

"He is exciting. He had a smile on his face from the minute he arrived at the camp."

Pocognoli added a strong leadership group helped him guide Union Saint-Gilloise to their first Belgian title in 90 years.

"Without leaders, you can't win anything," he said. "You need guys who are helping the staff bring the standard.

"We are really lucky that we have a lot of captains in this team.

"It is one of the reasons why I feel comfortable to come to Scotland as the gaffer because I know we have fantastic leaders who are committed to doing their best for their country."

Another of those is obviously captain Andy Robertson and Pocognoli said "it is fantastic" the Tottenham Hotspur left-back is set to equal Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps.

"We are really lucky in modern football to have a leader like him," he added.

Pocognoli has remained positive despite Scotland sitting third in Nations League Group B1 behind Switzerland and Slovenia and in danger of missing out on promotion.

He also learned a lot from each of his first four games in charge.

"We know what we need to improve, but it is always a short period of time - two days to prepare for the game," Pocognoli said.

Scotland need at least four points from their final two games to have a chance of a promotion play-off place.

Fail to get through and, depending on the draw, these next two games will be their last time together before the European Championship qualifiers.

"These two games, if we start the qualification in March, are the last package of games and we have to use it to be ready for the March camp," he added.

"If it is June, we have more time to prepare with friendlies. This camp is crucial for me in demanding the players try to impress me and do everything to improve."
